## 2026-09-17 — the wallet wrote every secret to disk world-readable first and narrowed afterwards; the window is closed on POSIX and a failed narrowing is no longer silent

**Status:** LANDED. Wallet-only increment (`wallet/main.cpp`), one new FAST gate, one new ledger row. No consensus, apply, wire, digest or genesis surface.

**Problem this change solves — two defects, both reproduced before anything was touched.**

**P-1, the window.** `write_bytes_file_0600` is the helper through which ten wallet commands put key material on disk. It created the file with `std::ofstream`, which opens at 0666 masked by the umask (0644 under the usual `umask 022`), wrote the complete secret into it, closed it, and only then called `std::filesystem::permissions(..., 0600)`. `strace` of a plain successful `shamir-split --out`, nothing injected and nothing mutated:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../s.json", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666) = 3
write(3, "DSS1\3\4\0\0\0\1Rs\231\227...", 24) = 24
fchmodat(AT_FDCWD, ".../s.json", 0600)                 = 0
```

Measured directly with an `LD_PRELOAD` observer on the narrowing call: *at narrowing time the file is mode 0644 with 60 bytes already written* — the whole share set. Any local process that can `open(2)` the path during that window reads the key material. Eight of the ten helper callers write PLAINTEXT key material (`shamir-split`, `shamir-rotate`, `account-create-batch`, `account-derive-batch`, `account-import`, `account-export`, `keyfile-recover`, `account-recover`; `keyfile-create` and `keyfile-reencrypt` write the encrypted DNK1 envelope). The final mode is 0600, so nothing that looks afterwards can see it: `keystore-audit`, the `mode_not_0600` hazard tag and the section 28 assertion landed earlier the same day all observe a correct file and report nothing. This is not exotic — it happens on every platform, every filesystem, every successful run.

**P-2, the silence.** The same function called `permissions(..., perm_ec)` and then `(void)perm_ec; return true;`. Under an `LD_PRELOAD` shim making `chmod`/`fchmod`/`fchmodat` return `EPERM` — standing in for a filesystem or platform where narrowing cannot happen (FAT/exFAT, some network and FUSE mounts, a path owned by another user) — `shamir-split --out`, `shamir-rotate --json` and `keyfile-create --json` each exited **0**, left the file at **644**, printed **nothing** on stderr, and reported success in their `--json` summary. The daemon binary already does the right thing here (`src/main.cpp::cmd_account_create`, plaintext `--out` branch: name the file, print `perm_ec.message()`, tell the operator to verify manually) — but note it is itself a P-1 instance, so it is a model for the error handling only, not for the ordering.

**The change.** In `write_bytes_file_0600`, on POSIX only: `::open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600)` **and** `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` before the first write. BOTH are needed and this is the measured part: `O_CREAT | O_TRUNC` with a mode does **not** narrow an existing file. Against the mutant that keeps the create mode and drops the `fchmod`, on a fresh create the observer reports `mode 0600 with 60 bytes already written`, and on a PRE-EXISTING 0644 target the same binary reports `mode 0644 with 60 bytes already written` and still ends at 0600. So the create mode alone leaves the entire window on every overwrite — the `--force` path and any second run — while a fresh-create test stays green. `fchmod` on the descriptor closes it on both paths with no TOCTOU. `O_NOFOLLOW` is deliberate and independent: without it a pre-existing symlink at the path is followed and the secret is written into whatever file it names, and the call sites' `fs::exists` checks are TOCTOU-racy, not a substitute. `O_CLOEXEC` keeps the descriptor out of any child.

On **Windows nothing is closed and the increment does not pretend otherwise**: the Windows branch keeps the previous `ofstream` code verbatim, because `_S_IREAD` / `_S_IWRITE` drive only `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` and the effective ACL comes by inheritance from the parent directory — already recorded in `docs/proofs/S005PassphraseKeyfile.md` F-4. The code comment and the ledger row say so in those words.

For P-2 the trailing `permissions` call is KEPT as the belt-and-braces step, its `error_code` is now CHECKED, and a failure emits the daemon's diagnostic (file, `perm_ec.message()`, `Verify manually (chmod 0600 / icacls).`) and is reported back to the caller through a new defaulted `bool* perms_narrowed_out`. A failing `fchmod` is reported the same way. The write still SUCCEEDS, the exit code is unchanged and the file is NOT deleted: destroying a `keyfile-recover` result the operator may be unable to regenerate is a worse outcome than a wide file they were told about. Seven commands that already print a `--json` summary on the write path now add `"perms_narrowed": false` to it when the narrowing failed — `shamir-rotate`, `keyfile-create`, `keyfile-reencrypt`, `keyfile-recover`, `account-recover`, and the two sites below. The field is emitted **only on failure**, so every success summary is byte-identical to what it was and no consumer, golden or documented shape changes; its absence carries no new promise, and the loud stderr diagnostic accompanies every `false`.

Two independent sites are routed through the hardened helper, both near drop-ins that already built a single buffer, with the `determ_secure_zero` moved after the call: `backup-create --shares-out` (the DSS1 Shamir share-set) and `keyfile-decrypt --out` (the decrypted plaintext node key). One Windows-only consequence, stated rather than hidden: the helper writes in binary mode, so `keyfile-decrypt --out` now emits LF where the old text-mode stream emitted CRLF on Windows; on POSIX the bytes are identical, and the daemon's JSON parser accepts both. The in-code "matches `save_node_key` byte-for-byte" note is corrected in place to say it is a POSIX statement.

**A correction owed to this log, which is append-only.** The 2026-09-17 entry on the shamir-rotate gate says, under "noticed and deliberately left alone", that `write_bytes_file_0600` *"has eleven call sites, every one of them writing key material"*. It has **ten** callers. **Eleven** was the count of `std::filesystem::permissions` sites in `wallet/main.cpp`, of which exactly **one** was inside the helper; the other ten were independent code each with its own `ofstream` → write → `permissions` → `(void)perm_ec` sequence, and they are **not** all key material — four of them write signed transactions (`cold-sign`, `sign-anon-tx`, `tx-batch-sign`, `param-change-build`). The true surface was twenty output paths, not ten, which is why a helper-only change would have fixed one narrowing site of eleven. After this increment there are nine `permissions` sites: one in the helper and eight independent.

**The gate.** New wrapper `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh`, **18 assertions**, added to the FAST `ONLY_PATTERN` in `tools/run_all.sh` — FAST membership is not automatic and without that line `ci_local` would not run it, exactly as it does not run `tools/test_wallet_shamir_rotate.sh`.

*Leg A, ordering (Linux, strace), against a **PRE-EXISTING 0644 target***, which is the path where the defect survives a create-mode-only fix; a gate that only tested a fresh create would test the wrong thing. The assertion is: among the mode-setting calls affecting that file between the creating open and the first `write` to that descriptor, **at least one exists and the last one sets 0600**. It does **not** assert on the mode argument of the `openat`: measured, `strace` prints `openat(..., O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0600) = 3` on a file that stayed 0644, so that assertion would gate the source text of the call rather than the property. It does not assert "no write precedes the openat" either — a write to fd N cannot precede the openat that returns N, which is a tautology. Path-based calls (`chmod` / `fchmodat` / `fchmodat2` naming the target) count alongside descriptor-based ones, or the widen-between mutant below would pass. The creating open is selected by `O_CREAT` **and** a mode **and** a return >= 0, since the target path also appears in non-creating opens and a failed open creates nothing. The trace set is behind a capability probe of the SET as well as the binary (the pattern landed the same day in `tools/test_light_outbox.sh`), includes `fchmodat2` (glibc >= 2.39 / Linux >= 6.6) and degrades without it, and SKIPs **by name** when strace, ptrace or the trace set is unavailable. A parser self-check removes the pre-write mode-setting lines and requires the same parse to answer RED.

*Leg B, fault injection (anywhere `LD_PRELOAD` and a C compiler work).* The wrapper generates and builds a shim making `chmod`/`fchmod`/`fchmodat` return `EPERM`, probes with a compiled program that `LD_PRELOAD` actually intercepts (it does not under macOS SIP, and there is no such mechanism on Windows) and SKIPs by name otherwise, then runs `shamir-rotate`, `backup-create` and `keyfile-decrypt` against pre-existing 0644 targets under it and asserts BOTH halves: the harm is real (the file is left at **644**) AND the command says so — the pre-write diagnostic, the final-narrowing diagnostic, the verify-manually line, and `"perms_narrowed": false` in the `--json` summary. A fourth block asserts the success path is unchanged: 0600, empty stderr, and **no** `perms_narrowed` field.

A SKIP prints `SKIP:` with the cause and does **not** increment the pass count.

**Mutants**, each applied ALONE, rebuilt, and restored + rebuilt clean afterwards. The harness refuses to report a verdict unless a marker it injects is present in the source AND the build log shows `wallet/main.cpp` recompiled and `determ-wallet` relinked — a harness in this project silently built an unmutated binary once.

| id | mutation | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | restore the `std::ofstream` create (the original shape) | RED leg A + leg B (pre-write diagnostic) |
| M2 | keep the create mode, DROP the `fchmod` | RED leg A + leg B (pre-write diagnostic) |
| M3 | restore `(void)perm_ec` | RED leg B (final-narrowing diagnostic) |
| M4 | `fchmod` moved to AFTER the write | RED leg A |
| M5 | create 0600, `chmod 0666`, write, `chmod 0600` | RED leg A |

M5 is the one that matters most: it ends at mode 0600, so it satisfies the section 28 assertion in `tools/test_wallet_shamir_rotate.sh` and leaves the window fully open. All five leave that gate GREEN, which is the measured statement that the final-mode assertion cannot see any of this. M2 is green on a fresh create and RED on the pre-existing target, which is why leg A uses the latter.

**Riders: none.** No unrelated code improved, no formatting sweep, no other command touched.

**What does NOT change.** No consensus accept rule, apply path, wire format, digest, genesis or state layout; no migration; no `src/`, `include/`, `light/` or `dapps/` file. No exit code changes on any path — a failed narrowing still exits 0. No file is deleted on a failed narrowing (considered and rejected: a `keyfile-recover` result may be unregenerable). No new CLI flag. Every success-path `--json` summary is byte-identical. `tools/test_wallet_shamir_rotate.sh` section 28 stays green: the final mode is unchanged by this work.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (1) `wallet/main.cpp:2279` — `account-import-many` writes one plaintext DAK1 keyfile PER RECORD inside a loop with a `determ_secure_zero` between records, so it needs an open-restricted-then-stream shape rather than a buffer swap; it is the named follow-up and it is plaintext key material. (2) The other seven independent `permissions` sites keep the old `ofstream` → narrow → `(void)perm_ec` sequence: `wallet/main.cpp:2311` (`account-import-many` summary), `:3215` (`backup-create --envelopes-out`, AEAD-wrapped), `:4207` (`keyfile-rotate`, whose staged tmp file is also created by `ofstream` at the umask mode and narrowed only after the atomic rename — so the wide file exists under the FINAL name), and `:9776`, `:10161`, `:10778`, `:23541` (`cold-sign`, `sign-anon-tx`, `tx-batch-sign`, `param-change-build` — signed transactions, not keys). (3) `wallet/main.cpp:19026` and `:19493` — two bare `::chmod(out_path, 0600)` calls that ignore their return; both write audit/history exports (account identifiers, not keys) and both carry a comment recording that a failed chmod deliberately does not fail the export. Prior decision, lower sensitivity, untouched. (4) The write-and-rename shape (create the temp at 0600, fsync, rename over the target) is the better end state and would also make the overwrite atomic; `keyfile-rotate` already has the rename half. Not bundled here. (5) Windows, per the above. (6) `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` documents the success-path `--json` shapes of the seven affected commands and is UNCHANGED, because the failure-only field falsifies none of those sentences; documenting `perms_narrowed` there is a seven-row edit to a CRLF file and is its own increment. (7) `docs/proofs/WalletRecoveryFlows.md` section 8 cites `wallet/main.cpp:639-919`, `:1607-1773`, `:3239-3483` and `:3553-3940` for four `cmd_*` functions; those ranges were already stale before this change and this change shifts them further. In-bounds line drift, which `tools/test_doc_citation_bounds.sh` deliberately does not check; not re-derived here. (8) `docs/SECURITY.md` records S-091 — `save_node_key` writes the node identity seed with a bare `ofstream` and **no** permission call at all (`src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key`) — as the same class at its limit. It stays OPEN and is not touched.

**Ledger.** New row **S-109** (`⚠ OPEN`, Medium) in `docs/SECURITY.md` covering P-1 and P-2 across the wallet output surface, stating what this increment mitigates and what it does not, and cross-referencing S-091. The summary Medium cell moves 10 to 11 and the Open total 33 to 34; `tools/test_security_ledger_coherence.sh` green. `docs/proofs/WalletRecoveryFlows.md` section 6.1(g) is corrected inline — the ORDERING was the substance of that row and it was wrong — and section 7 gains the new gate's row.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, **FAST 321 passed / 0 failed** (320 before; this increment adds one FAST wrapper), 16 doc guards green. `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` alone: 18 pass / 0 fail, 0 sections skipped on this box. Each of M1..M5 RED against the REBUILT binary on the leg named above, restored and rebuilt clean afterwards.

**Authority:** the standing verification doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` (provable security B3; assert at the layer where the rule lives; smallest increment that keeps the tree green AND truthful) and the node-/client-local backlog authorized under D19a, item (11) of the 2026-09-16 implementation sequence. No consensus decision is touched and none is implied. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-17. ## 2026-09-17 — the node identity seed was written world-readable; the permissions half of S-091 closes, the plaintext half does not

**Status:** LANDED. Shipped-source change in `src/crypto/keys.cpp` (POSIX only) plus a new FAST gate. **S-091 stays ⚠ OPEN** and no summary cell in `docs/SECURITY.md` moves: what closed is the file's permissions and the visibility of a failure, not the encryption the row exists for.

**Problem this change solves.** `crypto::save_node_key` writes the node identity's 32-byte RFC 8032 SEED — the key that stakes, signs blocks and IS the node's consensus identity — as plaintext hex in JSON, and until today it wrote it through a bare `std::ofstream`. `std::ofstream` creates at `0666 & ~umask`, so the file landed at **0644** under the default umask 022 and at **0666** under umask 000, and nothing narrowed it afterwards: unlike the wallet's `write_bytes_file_0600`, which at least chmods after the write, this path made **no permission call at all**. The containing directory came from `fs::create_directories` at `0777 & ~umask`, i.e. **0755**. The callers, confirmed by reading them rather than assuming: `determ init` (`src/main.cpp` `cmd_init`, the `if (fs::exists(kpath))` / else keygen block) and `determ start` on first run (`cmd_start`, the `if (!fs::exists(cfg.key_path))` block). The brief's line numbers for both were correct. Every other call site in the tree is inside a `test-*` selftest block.

**Reproduced first, executed, before anything was touched.** Against the binary built from HEAD on Linux x86_64 (transcript in the session's audit directory): `determ init --data-dir D` under umask 022 produced `D` at **755** and `D/node_key.json` at **644**, containing `"priv_seed": "<64 hex>"` in clear; `su -s /bin/sh nobody -c 'grep priv_seed …'` **printed the seed**. The same command under umask 000 produced **777** and **666**. Under `strace`, the only line touching the key was `openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../node_key.json", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666) = 3` and the count of mode-setting calls on descriptor 3 was **zero**. That trace is also the concrete instance of today's wave lesson: strace printed the mode argument `0666` for a file that ended up 0644, so the printed mode says nothing about what the kernel used.

**The change (`src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key`, POSIX arm only).** The file is created with `::open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600)` and then narrowed with `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` **before the first byte is written**, the body being written with a `::write` loop that handles `EINTR` and short writes. Both the create mode and the `fchmod` are load-bearing and neither implies the other: measured, `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC` with a mode does **not** narrow a file that already exists, so the create mode alone leaves the window open on every rewrite, while a `::chmod` by path after the write is both a TOCTOU window and a period in which the seed is on disk world-readable. `O_NOFOLLOW` matters because without it a symlink planted at the path is followed, which redirects the seed into a file of the attacker's choosing and aims the narrowing at the wrong inode. A directory that **this call creates** is narrowed to 0700 before the file exists inside it, on that directory's own descriptor (`::open(parent, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW)` then `::fchmod(dfd, 0700)`) rather than by path, for the same anti-TOCTOU reason. The Windows arm is byte-for-byte what it was.

**Decision 1 — only directories this call created are narrowed.** `fs::create_directories` is called on a path the operator may already own and use for other things: the data dir also holds `config.json`, `chain.json` and exports, and an operator may have deliberately made it group-readable for a monitoring account. Clamping an existing directory to 0700 from inside a keyfile writer is an invisible side effect on state this function does not own, and it can break a deliberate deployment. A directory that did not exist one syscall ago has no such claims on it and its entire purpose at that moment is to hold a node identity, so 0700 there is both safe and strictly better. The two-argument `fs::create_directories(p, ec)` reports whether a directory was actually created; the throwing one-argument form the old code used discarded exactly that fact. **The consequence is stated rather than hidden:** `determ init` creates its data dir **itself**, before calling `save_node_key`, so that directory stays at 0755. The key file inside it is 0600, so the seed is not exposed, but the directory listing is. Narrowing it belongs to `cmd_init` and is a separate increment; it is recorded below.

**Decision 2 — a failed narrowing throws, it does not warn.** `save_node_key` already throws on a write failure, so throwing is the established shape of this function and both callers already handle it (`cmd_start` catches and exits 1). Beyond precedent the choice is not close. A node identity is written **once** — both shipped callers skip keygen when the file exists — and then read on every start for the life of the deployment, so a stderr warning is seen at most once, in a provisioning shell that is usually non-interactive, and never again, while the exposure is permanent. Unlike a wallet recovery transcript, a node identity **can be regenerated at no cost**: refusing costs the operator one re-run after fixing the filesystem, where continuing costs a world-readable identity that stakes and signs blocks. The repo already fails closed on the sibling case — `generate_node_key` throws when the CSPRNG fails rather than writing a weak seed. And the refusal is reachable only at CREATION time, so no provisioned node can be bricked by it on restart.

**Decision 3 — `load_node_key` is unchanged and does NOT warn about a wide mode.** The container is the same JSON it always was, so an existing 0644 `node_key.json` still loads byte-identically and there is no migration; that is asserted, not assumed. It does not warn, for three reasons. The advice a warning could give is wrong: once a 0644 seed has existed on a shared host the remedy is ROTATION, not `chmod`, and telling the operator to chmod invites exactly the false comfort of tightening a leaked file. It is `Node`'s constructor path (`src/node/node.cpp`, `key_ = crypto::load_node_key(cfg_.key_path)`), so it runs on every node start and inside every in-process cluster fixture that constructs Nodes — the line would print into the FAST suite's output repeatedly and become noise. And it is behaviour change on the happy path of every already-provisioned node, which is a rider on a permissions increment. The honest place for it is the D2 src-side keyfile increment, which rewrites this container anyway and can offer a real migration.

**Windows: nothing is closed there and nothing is claimed.** `_S_IREAD | _S_IWRITE` on `_open` drives only `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` — it is not a mode and grants nobody anything; the file's ACL arrives by inheritance from the parent directory, and `std::filesystem::permissions` does not rewrite it either. `docs/proofs/S005PassphraseKeyfile.md` F-4 records exactly this for the wallet's keyfiles ("the actual NTFS ACL after the call is operator-environment-dependent"). Calling either here would look like a fix and change nothing measurable, so the Windows writer is left exactly as it was, including its TEXT-mode `ofstream` whose LF-to-CRLF translation is part of the existing on-disk bytes. The exposure stands on Windows and the gate SKIPs there **by name** rather than banking a pass it did not earn.

**Gate.** New FAST member `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh`, three legs, **7 wrapper assertions over 18 in-process ones**, all asserting OUTCOMES on the filesystem and never source text. Leg A is the in-process property test `determ test-node-key-perms` (18 assertions, 7 scenarios): a path whose parent does not exist yields a 0600 file in a 0700 directory under a fixed umask 022 where the defaults would be 0644 and 0755 — the umask is fixed deliberately, because under umask 077 a plain `ofstream` already yields 0600 and every mutant would survive; a parent the operator already owns is left exactly at 0755; an ALREADY-EXISTING 0666 key file is narrowed to 0600, with a fixture control proving the target really was 0666 first; a symlink planted at the path is refused and its target is untouched; the on-disk JSON is byte-identical to the pre-change writer and an existing 0644 file still loads with no migration and no mode rewrite; and an injected failure of either narrowing throws, leaving no seed in the unprotectable file. Leg B is the outcome of the shipped `determ init` under umask 022 **and** under umask 000 — a mode that is only right under a lucky umask is not a mitigation — with a control assertion that the file under test really does contain `priv_seed`. Leg C is the syscall-order property no in-process check can make: under `strace`, scoped to the one descriptor the key was opened on and bounded by its `close` so descriptor reuse cannot be misread, **among the mode-setting calls on that descriptor before its first write, at least one exists and the last one sets 0600**. Leg C deliberately does NOT assert on the mode argument of the `openat`, for the reason the reproduction above demonstrates. It sits behind a capability probe — strace present, Linux, ptrace permitted, and the trace SET accepted, since an strace that does not know a name in the set exits 1 without creating its `-o` file — in the shape `tools/test_light_outbox.sh` section C uses, with `fchmodat2` in the set because a newer glibc can route `fchmod(2)` through it, degrading to the set without it on an strace that does not know the name. Leg C also carries a self-check on its own PARSER, not on the product: the same parse over the same trace with the `fchmod` lines stripped must NOT answer "closed", or the assertion above would be vacuous.

**Mutants — five, each alone, each against the REBUILT binary, source restored and rebuilt clean afterwards.** Every mutant injected a unique marker string and the harness refused to report a verdict unless that marker was found **both** in the patched source and, by `strings`, in the LINKED BINARY; a harness that silently builds unmutated code turns a green gate into a false kill, which happened to a harness earlier in this project. **M1** restores the pre-fix `std::ofstream` create: RED, 3 pass / 4 fail — leg A's file-mode, rewrite, symlink and injection assertions, leg B at both umasks (644 and 666), and leg C. **M2** keeps the `O_CREAT` mode and drops only the `fchmod`, leaving the injection arm intact: RED, 5 pass / 2 fail — killed **only** by the existing-file property and by leg C, exactly as predicted, since a fresh file still lands at 0600 and leg B alone would have passed it. **M3** leaves the created directory at 0755: RED on leg A's directory assertion. **M4** swallows both narrowing failures: RED on all four failure-reporting assertions. **M5** creates 0600, widens to 0666, writes the seed, then narrows back to 0600 — it ends at the right mode and passes every mode assertion in legs A and B, and is killed by leg C alone, which reports `open 600,666`. M5 is the mutant that a weaker ordering assertion (or any final-state assertion) would let through, and it is why leg C is written as "the LAST mode-setting call before the first write" rather than "some call sets 0600". Additionally, and unplanned, the whole pre-fix `save_node_key` was restored and the gate run against it: **3 pass / 4 fail**, 11 of the 18 in-process assertions RED.

**Riders: none.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no genesis field, no migration, no on-disk format change — the JSON container is asserted byte-identical. `load_node_key` is unchanged in behaviour. The only other shipped-source edit is the new `test-node-key-perms` selftest block plus its usage line in `src/main.cpp`, and two guarded POSIX includes.

**What remains OPEN in S-091 after this, by name.** The seed is still **PLAINTEXT hex inside JSON**, where the wallet ships the DWE2 Argon2id + AES-256-GCM envelope and the light client its binary DAK1/DNK1 containers; that is the D2 remainder "node_key.json stays src-owned JSON" (D2-DEFERRED(src)), it is owner-gated, and it is why the row stays ⚠ OPEN and the ledger summary does not move. Also open: nothing at all is mitigated on Windows; `load_node_key` does not warn about an existing wide mode; the `determ init` data dir stays 0755; an ancestor directory that `save_node_key` created on the way to the leaf is not narrowed (only the leaf is), which is harmless while the leaf is 0700 but is worth knowing; `O_NOFOLLOW` guards only the FINAL path component, so an attacker who controls an ancestor directory can still redirect through a symlinked component; `O_NOFOLLOW` does not stop a HARD link either, so an attacker with write access to the containing directory can still aim the write at an inode of their choosing (the narrowing then fails with EPERM and throws whenever that inode is not ours, and `O_EXCL` — which would close it outright — is not used because the rewrite-narrows-an-existing-file property this increment gates requires the rewrite path to work); a pre-existing `node_key.json` is still truncated by `O_TRUNC` before anything is checked, exactly as the old writer did, so a failed narrowing on a path that already held a key destroys it — unreachable from either shipped caller, both of which skip when the file exists; and the seed still passes through a `std::string` and an `nlohmann::json` that are not zeroized, exactly as before, which the D2 container increment is the place to fix.

**On the test-only fault injection.** `DETERM_NODE_KEY_INJECT=fchmod|dirchmod` makes the corresponding narrowing report failure. It exists because a failed narrowing cannot be produced from outside the process on the platforms this is gated on — the test runs as the file's owner and an owner's `fchmod` on a local filesystem does not fail — so without it the "report the failure" rule would have had no gate that can go RED, i.e. no gate. It follows the shape `light/outbox.cpp` already uses (`DETERM_LIGHT_OUTBOX_INJECT`), it is one `getenv` when unset, and it can only ever turn a success into a REPORTED FAILURE, never the reverse, so it cannot be used to weaken a permission.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (1) `src/main.cpp` `cmd_init` creates the data dir with `fs::create_directories(data_dir)` at 0755 and never narrows it; the seed inside is 0600 after this change, but the directory listing is world-readable. Narrowing it is a change to a directory that also holds `config.json`, `chain.json` and exports and affects roughly thirty in-tree fixtures, so it is its own increment. (2) `wallet/main.cpp`'s `write_bytes_file_0600` still DISCARDS the chmod error — `(void)perm_ec; return true;` — across eleven call sites, all writing key material; it also chmods by PATH after the write, the TOCTOU shape this increment removed from the node key. The same descriptor-based treatment belongs there and is a separate increment (already recorded in the 2026-09-17 shamir-rotate entry as item 1b). (3) `src/main.cpp`'s `cmd_account_create` plaintext-file path (`determ account create --out`) writes the account privkey with `std::ofstream` and then `std::filesystem::permissions(...)` — the same create-wide-then-narrow window this change closed for the node key, on a file that also holds a private key. (4) `docs/SECURITY.md` states the FAST tier is "299 wrappers" in two places where it is 320 before this change; pre-existing drift this increment did not create and does not correct, since correcting it means editing two large shared paragraphs that another track may be touching today. (5) The repo carries two incompatible SKIP conventions (skip without incrementing `pass_count`, as `test_light_outbox` does and this gate does, versus skip as a banked pass); this gate entrenches the first.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, **FAST 321 passed / 0 failed** (320 before, plus `test_node_key_perms`), 16 doc guards green. `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` directly: 7 pass / 0 fail clean; RED under each of M1–M5 with the per-mutant counts above; 3 pass / 4 fail against the fully restored pre-fix `save_node_key`. Every mutant verdict was read only after the build was confirmed to succeed AND the marker was confirmed present in the linked binary.

**Authority:** D19a (the node-/client-local backlog, `docs/SECURITY.md` S-091 "authorized 2026-09-16 (D19a)"), for the PERMISSIONS half only. The encryption half is D2 src-side and owner-gated; it is not taken here and S-091 is not closed. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-17. This entry is append-only per convention and carries no tier marker in its body.

## 2026-09-17 — determ-light secret seeds can be supplied off the command line (S-110); the raw flags stay, and now say so

**Status:** LANDED. Client-tooling increment, ADDITIVE ONLY. No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no migration.

**Problem this change solves, reproduced before it was touched.** Every `determ-light` subcommand that takes a private seed took it as a command-line ARGUMENT: `pq-sign-tx --mldsa-seed <hex32> [--ed-seed <hex32>]`, `pq-address --mldsa-seed <hex32>`, `pq-transfer --mldsa-seed <hex32>`, and `build-shield` / `build-unshield --blind-seed <hex>`. A running process's argument vector has three readers the operator did not choose. `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable for the lifetime of the command; `ps -ww -o args=` prints the same line to every user on the host; and the operator's interactive shell appends the command verbatim to the history file, where it outlives the process. For an ML-DSA or Ed25519 seed the hex string IS the private key. The reproduction (executed, transcript in the audit dir, not an argument from reading the source) started a `pq-sign-tx` whose `--out` was a FIFO so it blocked in `open(2)` after signing, read the seed out of `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and out of `ps` from a second process, showed the same seed landing in a `$HISTFILE`, and then rebuilt a valid `PQ_TRANSFER` from the leaked seed — the reader signs as that identity.

**The change.** Every one of those flags gained a `--*-seed-from <source>` twin — `--mldsa-seed-from`, `--ed-seed-from`, `--blind-seed-from` — taking `file:<path>` (first line, whitespace-trimmed), `env:<NAME>`, or `prompt` (stdin, terminal echo disabled). This deliberately MIRRORS `determ-wallet keyfile-create --passphrase-from` (`wallet/main.cpp::passphrase_from_source`): same three source forms, same diagnostic wording, same exit code 1 on a bad source. That helper is in the wallet binary's own translation unit and `determ-light` is a separate CMake target that does not link it, so the parsing is re-implemented in the new `light/seed_source.cpp` rather than dragging `wallet/main.cpp` across a binary boundary. One deliberate divergence: the wallet strips only CR/LF because a passphrase may contain spaces; a hex seed cannot, so the seed reader trims ASCII whitespace at both ends. Passing both forms of one seed is refused rather than silently preferring one. Resolved seed material — the hex string, the decoded 32 bytes, the blinding vector — is `determ_secure_zero`d by a scope guard on every exit path including the throwing ones, matching `light/keyfile.cpp`'s existing discipline; `light/` had no zeroing on this path before.

**What does NOT change, stated plainly because the ledger row depends on it.** The raw `--mldsa-seed` / `--ed-seed` / `--blind-seed` flags still exist and still work: same accepted inputs, same output bytes, same exit codes. Removing them is an owner decision, not a track's — `tools/test_light_pq_sign.sh`, `tools/test_pq_transfer_e2e.sh` and `tools/test_light_ct_tx.sh` all drive them, and those three are the regression lock that the old form is unchanged, so they were deliberately NOT converted. An operator who keeps typing the raw flag keeps the whole exposure. The only behavioural change on that path is a named `WARNING[seed-on-command-line]` line on stderr naming the process table, the shell history file and the `-from` alternative — a warning, not a refusal, exit code untouched. So S-110 is recorded `🟠 Partially mitigated`, not closed. Two smaller diagnostic changes ride on the same path and are stated rather than hidden: a malformed hex seed now names the offending flag (`--mldsa-seed is not valid hex (odd hex length)`) where it previously surfaced the bare `from_hex` message, and `build-shield` / `build-unshield` now decode the blinding hex before loading the keyfile, so when BOTH are bad the hex error is reported first. Exit code 1 in every one of those cases, before and after.

**Gate.** `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh`, new, added to the FAST `ONLY_PATTERN` alternation in `tools/run_all.sh` (membership there is explicit, not automatic); FAST rises 320 -> 321. 28 assertions in five groups, each asserted at the layer where its rule lives. (A) `--mldsa-seed-from file:` produces BYTE-IDENTICAL output to `--mldsa-seed` with the same seed for `pq-address`, `pq-transfer` and hybrid `pq-sign-tx`, and the `-from`-signed tx verifies through `pq-verify-tx` — the equivalence that makes the new form usable. (B) `env:` and `prompt` agree with the raw form, `env:` reads the variable it was NAMED and not another, and a missing file, an empty file, an unset variable, an unknown source scheme, both forms at once and an odd-length or short hex seed are each refused with a named diagnostic and exit 1 — on the raw flag as well as the `-from` one. (C) the raw form emits the named warning and still exits 0 with correct output; the `-from` form writes nothing to stderr; the hybrid `--ed-seed` gets its own warning naming `--ed-seed-from`. (D) the property itself, read from the kernel and not grepped out of the source: with `--mldsa-seed-from` the seed is ABSENT from the running child's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, and the control shows the raw flag DOES put it there in the same window. Both children are pinned in a deterministic window by a FIFO and the wait is on `/proc/<pid>/comm`, which no argv edit can forge; the section prints `SKIP:` by name where `/proc/self/cmdline` does not exist rather than banking a pass. (E) `--blind-seed-from` round-trips byte-identically for `build-shield` / `build-unshield` and the raw form warns.

**Mutants, each alone, each RED against the REBUILT binary, source restored and rebuilt clean afterwards.** M1 `-from` silently falls back to treating its argument as raw hex — RED on A1/A2/A3/A4, B1..B5, B7..B9, C3, D1, D3, E1, E3, E4, E5. M2 the warning is dropped on the raw form — RED on C1, C4, E2. M3 a short or odd-length hex seed is accepted (zero-padded) — RED on B6, B7, B11, B12. M4 `env:` reads a fixed variable instead of the one named — RED on B3. M5 the `-from` path writes the resolved seed back into the process's own argument block — RED on D1. The harness REFUSES a verdict unless the injected marker is found in the source, `cmake --build` exits 0, AND the `determ-light` mtime strictly advances; it aborts if the baseline or the restored tree is not green.

**A measured lesson about the /proc assertion, recorded because it nearly banked a false pass.** The first version of group D pinned the child by making the `file:` SOURCE a FIFO, so the snapshot of `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` was taken while the process was still blocked reading the seed — i.e. BEFORE the seed existed in the process at all. Against that window M5 stayed GREEN: an argv write-back that happens after the read is invisible to a sample taken before it. The gate now takes the `-from` window strictly AFTER the signature (ordinary file as the source; the FIFO is `--out`, which `pq-sign-tx` opens only once the envelope is built), and M5 is RED. The general form of the lesson: for a "secret is absent from X" property, the sample must be taken at or after the last moment the code could have put it there.

**Riders.** None. No file outside `light/`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/run_all.sh`, the new wrapper and the three doc/ledger loci is touched.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (1) `determ-wallet` takes private key material on the command line in nine places and is NOT changed here — `cmd_keyfile_create --priv` (`wallet/main.cpp:3304`), `cmd_account_import --priv` (`:1633`), `cmd_message_sign --priv` (`:6103`), `cmd_account_derive_batch --seed` (`:1383`), `cmd_create_recovery --seed` (`:5884`), `cmd_shamir_split_raw --secret` (`:431`), `cmd_backup_create --secret` (`:2845`), `cmd_merkle_proof --key` (`:14524`) and `cmd_rpc_auth --secret` (`:23851`). Ironically `keyfile-create` is the very command whose `--passphrase-from` this increment mirrors: it takes the passphrase safely and the Ed25519 seed unsafely, in the same argument list. (2) The `determ` daemon does the same in six places — `cmd_account_create --passphrase` (`src/main.cpp:5857`), `cmd_account_decrypt --passphrase` (`:5969`) and the `--priv` of `cmd_submit_param_change` (`:6133`), `cmd_submit_merge_event` (`:6263`), `cmd_submit_dapp_register` (`:6346`) and `cmd_submit_dapp_call` (`:6472`). (3) `determ-light verify-selection-offline --seed-hex` (`light/main.cpp:10746`) is the PUBLIC `cumulative_rand` beacon seed, authenticated by `verify-rand`, not a secret — left alone on purpose. (4) `file:` does not check the seed file's permissions, and `env:` is still readable at `/proc/<pid>/environ` by the same UID; both match the wallet's `--passphrase-from` exactly and are documented in `light/seed_source.hpp` rather than silently diverged from. (5) `docs/SECURITY.md` §6 still says the FAST tier holds "299 wrappers"; that sentence was already false at 320 before this change and is not this increment's to re-derive. (6) The three existing tests now print the new warning into the suite log; that is the intended effect of using the raw flag and was not suppressed.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh --jobs 1` on **Linux x86_64** — configure + build **7 targets**, **FAST 321 passed / 0 failed** (320 before; +1 is `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh`), **16 doc guards green**. Gate alone: 28 pass / 0 fail; 27 pass / 1+ fail under each of M1..M5.

**Authority:** the standing doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` — provable security (B3), new behaviour ships with a falsify-on-mutant gate at the layer where the rule lives, smallest increment that keeps the tree green AND truthful. No owner decision is required or implied by an additive flag; the one decision this increment explicitly does NOT take is removing the raw `--*-seed` flags, which is the owner's.

## 2026-09-17 — integration pass over the three permissions increments: a daemon abort introduced by one of them, and three corrections this log owes itself

**Status:** LANDED. Fixes a regression introduced earlier in this same wave, hardens two of the wave's own gates, opens S-111, and corrects three false statements in the three entries above.

**Problem this change solves — 1: `determ init` aborted and then silently reported success over an empty node identity.** The entry above that closes the permissions half of S-091 made `save_node_key` THROW when it cannot narrow the seed file to 0600. Its stated justification says "both callers already handle it (`cmd_start` catches and exits 1)". `cmd_init` does NOT. And the throw fires after `O_TRUNC` has already created the file, so a zero-byte `node_key.json` is left behind. Reproduced, executed, before this fix: `DETERM_NODE_KEY_INJECT=fchmod determ init --data-dir D` terminated with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'` and **exit 134**, i.e. SIGABRT and the terminate handler's text rather than the diagnostic that was carefully written. The retry the diagnostic asks for then hit `cmd_init`'s `if (fs::exists(kpath))` guard, printed **"Key already exists (skipping keygen)"**, exited **0**, and told the operator to run `determ start` — which failed with `parse error at line 1, column 1: attempting to parse an empty input`, naming neither the key file nor the permission problem. A crash followed by a false success followed by an unrelated-looking fatal, on the identity a node stakes and signs with. This was introduced by this wave and would have shipped.

**The fix.** `::unlink(path)` before every POSIX throw in `save_node_key` that fires after the file exists — the fchmod-failure throw, the write-failure throw and the close-failure throw — so nothing is left for an exists-guard to misread. `cmd_init`'s keygen is wrapped in the try/catch shape `cmd_start` has always had, so the refusal exits 1 with its own text. After the fix, measured: exit **1**, the real diagnostic on stderr, **no leftover file**, and the retry genuinely regenerates a 165-byte 0600 key that `determ start` loads.

**Problem 2: the gate could not see it.** The selftest's assertion was `slurp(p).find("priv_seed") == npos` — "no seed was written to the unprotectable file" — which a zero-byte leftover satisfies exactly. It now also asserts `!fs::exists(p)`, the form the sibling directory-failure case two blocks below was already using. Mutant N1 (drop the `unlink`, rebuild): **RED** on that assertion, GREEN before it existed.

**Problem 3: one of the wave's two strace legs could not see a path-based widen.** `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg C matched only descriptor-first-argument calls (`fchmod(fd, …)`), while its sibling `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` leg A counts path-based `chmod`/`fchmodat` on the target as well and says why. Demonstrated on the exact adversarial trace — create 0600, `fchmod(fd,0600)`, `chmod(path,0666)`, write, `chmod(path,0600)`, final mode 0600 so every mode assertion in the tree passes — the descriptor-only parser answers **closed** and the corrected one answers **open**. Leg C now counts both, and its own non-vacuity self-check strips both spellings rather than only one. Mutant N2 (a path-based widen inside `save_node_key`, rebuilt) turns leg C RED with `parse said: open 600,666`.

**Problem 4: one of the wave's gates could report PASS having asserted nothing.** `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` printed `PASS:` and exited 0 when the wallet binary was absent, and its verdict was `fail_count == 0` alone — so on a box with neither strace/ptrace nor a C compiler both sections SKIP and `0 pass / 0 fail` would have printed PASS. In the gate whose own increment exists because a permission check could not fail, that is not acceptable. It now fails closed on a missing binary and refuses to report success when `pass_count` is zero. Mutant N3 (point `DETERM_WALLET_BIN` at a nonexistent path): **RED**, exit 1, where it previously printed PASS.

**Problem 5: a spin in one of the two hand-rolled write loops.** `src/crypto/keys.cpp` looped forever on a `write()` returning 0 for a positive count; `wallet/main.cpp`'s sibling writer, written the same day by a different track, guards exactly that case and says so in a comment. Impossible on a regular file, and a hang on the secret path is worse than an error, so the guard is now in both. This is the first visible cost of two independent hand-rolled restricted writers with nothing shared between them; a `write_all` primitive in `include/` is the obvious remedy and is NOT done here.

**Corrections this log owes itself, since it is append-only.**
(a) The S-091 entry's item (2) says `wallet/main.cpp`'s `write_bytes_file_0600` "still DISCARDS the chmod error — `(void)perm_ec; return true;` — across eleven call sites, all writing key material", chmods "by PATH after the write", and that fixing it "is a separate increment". Every clause was already false when that entry landed, because the wallet increment is its parent commit: `perm_ec` is checked, the narrowing is `::fchmod` on the descriptor BEFORE the first write, there are twelve callers not eleven, and four of the independent sites write signed transactions rather than key material. The entry two above it states the corrected counts and is the one to read.
(b) All three entries of this wave, and all three commit messages, record **"FAST 321 passed / 0 failed (320 before)"**. That is true of each increment measured alone in its own worktree. In the integrated linear history the counts are 320 → 321 → 322 → 323, and HEAD is **323**.
(c) The wallet entry's "what does not change" says "no exit code changes". `O_NOFOLLOW` on the output path means a symlinked `--out` (including `--out /dev/stdout`) now fails with `ELOOP` and exit 1 where it previously succeeded. That is the flag's purpose and no test or document used a symlinked output, but it IS an exit-code change and the entry should have said so. The sibling increment made the same change and did document it.

**S-111 opened.** `determ account create --out`, the daemon's plaintext branch, is the same P-1 defect on plaintext key material in the shipped daemon, and it is the one site of its class that S-109, S-110 and S-091 all leave uncovered. Reproduced: the creating `openat` takes mode 0666, the JSON carrying `"privkey"` in clear is written, and the narrowing to 0600 comes last; final mode 600, so nothing after the fact can see it. Its P-2 half is already correct there — it is the site the wallet increment copied its diagnostic from. Not fixed here; this wave was scoped to three other files, and an increment that fixes it should carry its own gate.

**What does not change.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no genesis field, no migration. The on-disk `node_key.json` format is byte-identical and `load_node_key` is untouched; an existing 0644 key still loads. No wallet or `determ-light` source changes in this entry.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** The three new gates entrench three different missing-binary conventions — `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` now fails closed, `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` fails through `tools/common.sh`, `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh` exits 0 with no marker — and the repo already had two incompatible SKIP conventions before today; a `skip_count` in the suite summary is the fix and it is a repo-wide convention change. `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh`'s `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` sample is bounded above by a FIFO but has no lower bound on the child's progress, so its "strictly after the signature" claim is stronger than the code; it held on every observed run and the mutant that would exercise it writes argv early. `docs/SECURITY.md` still describes the FAST tier as "299 wrappers" in two places where it is 323. `src/crypto/keys.cpp`'s `blob` still holds the seed in an unzeroized `std::string`. The `determ init` data directory is still created 0755.

Mutants N1, N2 and N3 each RED against the rebuilt binary and restored clean afterwards; the leg C parser change additionally demonstrated offline on the adversarial trace above.

## 2026-09-18 — the daemon's `account create --out` wrote the private key into a world-readable file and narrowed it afterwards; the POSIX window closes on both branches, and a selftest that banked a pass on Windows stops doing so

**Status:** LANDED. Two changes in `src/main.cpp`; one new gate (`tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` plus its in-process `determ test-account-create-perms`) added to the FAST alternation in `tools/run_all.sh`; one row in `docs/SECURITY.md` moved to partially mitigated; two rows in `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md`; and one header sentence in `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` corrected. No consensus, apply, wire, digest, genesis or state surface; no migration; no new dependency.

**Problem 1 — the window, reproduced before anything was touched.** `determ account create --out F` is the DAEMON binary's key-generation command. Both of its file branches wrote through a bare `std::ofstream`, which creates at `0666 & ~umask` — 0644 under the usual umask 022 — filled the file with the complete secret, and only then called `std::filesystem::permissions(..., 0600)`. `strace` of a plain successful run against the binary built from HEAD, umask 022, nothing injected and nothing mutated:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../plain.json", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666) = 3
write(3, "{\n  \"address\": \"0x12019ee1f40ee7"..., 243) = 243
close(3)
fchmodat(AT_FDCWD, ".../plain.json", 0600)                        = 0
```

The 243 bytes are the JSON carrying the fresh 32-byte Ed25519 seed as `"privkey"` in clear. Measured directly with an `LD_PRELOAD` observer on the narrowing call: *at narrowing time the file is mode 0644 with all 243 bytes already written*. With the narrowing denied by a second shim, in a traversable directory, `su -s /bin/sh nobody -c 'grep privkey …'` **printed the key**. The FINAL mode is 0600, so `keystore-audit`, the `mode_not_0600` hazard tag and every after-the-fact check in the tree see a correct file — which is why this survived S-004, S-109, S-110 and S-091. The `--passphrase` branch a few dozen lines below had the identical ordering defect on its AES-256-GCM container. This is the same P-1 defect S-109 records for the wallet, in the shipped daemon, on plaintext key material; it was opened as S-111 by the 2026-09-17 integration pass and left unfixed there.

**Problem 2 — a selftest that banked a pass having asserted nothing.** `determ test-node-key-perms` printed its Windows `SKIP:` line and then, immediately after it, the terminal marker `PASS: node-key-perms all assertions` and returned 0. `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg A greps for exactly that marker, and legs B and C already skip on Windows, so on that platform the wrapper's verdict was 1 pass / 0 fail — green forever, whatever `save_node_key` did. The wrapper's own header claimed "nothing is asserted and nothing is claimed" there, which was true of legs B and C and false of leg A. A gate that cannot fail on a platform is the defect two of the 2026-09-17 increments existed to remove.

**The change (1) — one restricted writer for both branches of `cmd_account_create`.** `write_account_file_0600(out_path, data)` creates with `::open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600)` **and** `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` before the first byte, then writes with a loop that handles `EINTR` and short writes and refuses to spin on `write() == 0`. Both calls are load-bearing and neither implies the other, which is the measured part: `O_CREAT | O_TRUNC` with a mode does **not** narrow a file that already exists, so the create mode alone leaves the entire window open on every overwrite while a fresh-create test stays green. `::fchmod` on the descriptor closes the create path and the overwrite path with nothing to race. `O_NOFOLLOW` is independent: without it a symlink planted at the path is followed, which both writes the key into whatever file it names and aims the narrowing at the wrong inode. `O_CLOEXEC` keeps the descriptor out of any child. Both branches are byte-for-byte identical on the wire — the plaintext JSON and the `DETERM-ACCOUNT-V1 <addr>` + blob container are the same bytes as before, and `account decrypt` reads them unchanged.

**On Windows nothing is closed and the increment does not pretend otherwise.** `_S_IREAD | _S_IWRITE` on `_open` drives only `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`, and the effective ACL arrives by inheritance from the parent directory — recorded in `docs/proofs/S005PassphraseKeyfile.md` F-4. The Windows arm therefore keeps the previous `std::ofstream` **text-mode** behaviour verbatim, CRLF translation included, so its output stays byte-identical there too; the sibling wallet increment switched to binary mode and changed its Windows bytes, and that is deliberately not repeated. The code comment, the usage text, the ledger row and this entry all say the window is closed on POSIX only.

**P-2, the reporting, was already correct at this site and is UNCHANGED — deliberately.** This is the one place in the tree that checked `perm_ec` and printed a named warning; `wallet/main.cpp::write_bytes_file_0600` copied its diagnostic from here. The trailing `std::filesystem::permissions` call, its `error_code` check and both lines of the diagnostic are the previous ones verbatim. A narrowing that fails before the write is reported with the wording the wallet's sibling writer uses and **the write continues**: exit codes do not change. REFUSING there instead — the shape `src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key` uses for the node identity seed — was written, gated and then **removed from this increment before commit**. It is defensible (a freshly generated key costs nothing to regenerate), but it is an exit-code change on a shipped command, it is separable from the write window this increment closes, and it needed a `getenv` fault-injection hook on the shipped key-write path to be gated in process. CLAUDE.md records that two verified slashing cores were sunk by riders, one of them an exit-code change. It is named as the S-111 remainder instead.

**The ONE exit-code change, stated rather than hidden.** `O_NOFOLLOW` makes `--out` naming a SYMLINK (including `--out /dev/stdout`) fail `ELOOP` with exit 1 on both branches, where it previously followed the link and succeeded. Nothing in the tree used a symlinked `--out`. The `determ` usage text and the `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` row for `account create` now say so; the wallet increment made the same change without documenting it and had to be corrected the next day.

**The change (2) — the platform-skip arm banks no pass.** `test-node-key-perms`' Windows arm prints a `SKIP:` marker **instead of** the terminal PASS marker and returns 1, and the new `test-account-create-perms` does the same, so no caller can read success out of either. On a platform where the property cannot be observed the honest answer is "no result", and between silently answering yes and loudly answering no the repo fails closed — which is what `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` already does. `DETERM_TEST_FORCE_PLATFORM_SKIP` makes that arm reachable on POSIX, inside the `test-*` blocks only, because a box that cannot build for Windows could otherwise check this property only by reading the source.

**The gate.** New in-process `determ test-account-create-perms` (**22 assertions**) plus the new wrapper `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` (**29 assertions**), added to the FAST `ONLY_PATTERN` alternation in `tools/run_all.sh` — FAST membership is an explicit alternation, not automatic, and without that edit `ci_local` would never run it.

*In process,* asserted as outcomes on the filesystem, on the command's exit code, on its diagnostics and on the bytes of the container, never as source text: a fresh target is 0600 and the container, the success line and the empty stderr are unchanged, with a control that the file really holds the key and that the key derives the address in it; a **PRE-EXISTING 0644** target is narrowed to 0600 on **both** branches — the case the `O_CREAT` mode argument provably cannot reach — and `O_TRUNC` really replaced the stale bytes; the envelope still decrypts with the address as AAD; a symlink planted at the path is refused by both branches and its target is untouched; and under umask 000 both branches still land 0600, so the mode is chosen and not inherited. Deliberately NOT in process: the syscall ORDER, which a process cannot observe about itself, and a narrowing that genuinely FAILS, which this process cannot produce — it owns the file it writes and an owner's `fchmod` does not fail. Faking the second with an injection hook would have put test-only code on the shipped key-write path for a property this increment does not change.

*Leg B of the wrapper, ordering (Linux, strace), against a **PRE-EXISTING 0644 target** on both branches*: among the mode-setting calls affecting that file between the creating open and the first `write` to that descriptor, at least one EXISTS and the LAST one sets 0600. It does **not** assert on the mode argument of the `openat` — strace prints `openat(..., O_CREAT, 0600)` whether or not the kernel used it, and the pre-fix trace above prints 0666 for a file that ended at 0644. Path-based calls (`chmod` / `fchmodat` / `fchmodat2` naming the target) are counted alongside descriptor-based `fchmod`, and the non-vacuity self-check strips BOTH spellings; a descriptor-only parser reports `create 0600; fchmod(fd,0600); chmod(path,0666); write; chmod(path,0600)` as closed with the window fully open. The trace set is behind a capability probe of the SET as well as the binary, includes `fchmodat2` and degrades without it.

*Leg C, fault injection*: an `LD_PRELOAD` shim makes `chmod` / `fchmod` / `fchmodat` return `EPERM`, and the shipped command runs under it against a **pre-existing 0644 target** on both branches — with the fix in place a FRESH create under that shim still lands 0600 from the create mode, so a fresh-create leg could not show the harm at all. It asserts BOTH halves: the harm is real (the file is left at **644** with `"privkey"` in it) AND both named diagnostics appear — the pre-write one and the `perm_ec` one — plus the verify-manually line, plus that the exit code did **not** change. A fourth block asserts the success path is unchanged: 0600, empty stderr, exit 0.

*Leg D*: neither this gate's nor `test-node-key-perms`' platform-skip arm prints a terminal PASS marker, each names itself as a SKIP, and each exits non-zero.

Every leg SKIPs BY NAME where its capability is absent, a SKIP does not increment the pass count, the wrapper fails closed when the binary is missing, and the verdict requires `pass_count > 0` as well as `fail_count == 0`.

**Mutants**, each applied ALONE, rebuilt, then restored and rebuilt clean. The harness REFUSES a verdict unless a marker it injects is present in the SOURCE, the build SUCCEEDED, and the marker is present in the RELINKED BINARY. The first run of this harness REFUSED its first verdict for exactly that reason — the marker was a local `const char*` that `-O3` discarded, so it was present in the source and absent from the binary — and the marker was changed to a file-scope `extern "C"` definition before any mutant was judged. That is the check working, not a formality.

| id | mutation | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | restore the pre-fix `std::ofstream` create-then-narrow on both branches | RED — in-process (symlink refusal) AND leg B (ordering, both branches) AND leg C (the pre-write diagnostic) |
| M2 | keep the 0600 create mode, DROP the `::fchmod` before the write | RED — leg B on both branches (`got: none`) AND leg C; **green on every in-process mode assertion**, which is why leg B runs against a pre-existing target |
| M3 | `::fchmod` moved to AFTER the write (final mode still 0600) | RED — leg B on both branches (`got: none`) |
| M4 | create 0600, `fchmod(fd,0600)`, widen the PATH to 0666, write, narrow back by path (final mode 0600) | RED — leg B on both branches (`got: 666`) |
| M5 | drop the `perm_ec` check and its named warning | RED — leg C (the final-narrowing diagnostic and the verify-manually line, on both branches) |
| M6 | restore the Windows-banked `PASS: node-key-perms all assertions` in the skip arm | RED — leg D (all three assertions for `test-node-key-perms`) |

M4 is the one that matters most: it ends at mode 0600, so every final-mode assertion in the tree is green on it, and only the ordering leg that counts path-based calls kills it. M1 and M2 are green on every in-process MODE assertion too, because the trailing `permissions` call fixes the final mode in both — the measured statement that no after-the-fact check can see this defect.

**Riders: none.** No unrelated code improved, no formatting sweep, no other command touched, and the refusal-on-unprotectable policy described above was deliberately backed out rather than bundled.

**What does NOT change.** No consensus accept rule, apply path, wire format, digest, genesis field, state layout or migration. No `wallet/`, `light/`, `dapps/`, `include/` or `sim/` file. The on-disk containers of both branches are byte-identical, so `account decrypt` and every existing keyfile still work. Exit codes are unchanged everywhere except the symlinked `--out` named above. No new CLI flag. `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` keeps all three of its legs and its Linux verdict is unchanged; on Windows it now goes RED instead of falsely green, and only its header sentence was edited to say so.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** **(1) The S-111 remainder, which is why the row is PARTIALLY mitigated and not closed.** (a) Windows: the `#ifdef _WIN32` arm of `write_account_file_0600` (`src/main.cpp:5915`) is the previous `std::ofstream` verbatim and the window there is exactly as wide as it was. (b) When the narrowing genuinely fails the command still writes the plaintext key into a file it could not protect and exits 0 with two warnings; refusing instead is the separable increment described above. **(2) Every remaining path in `src/` that puts secret material on disk, enumerated rather than assumed.** There are exactly two file-writing sites for key material in `src/`, and after this increment both are the same shape: `src/main.cpp` `write_account_file_0600` (this one) and `src/crypto/keys.cpp` `save_node_key` (POSIX-fixed 2026-09-17). `save_node_key`'s Windows arm (`src/crypto/keys.cpp:238`) is unfixed for the same reason as (1a), and the seed it writes is still PLAINTEXT hex inside JSON — S-091 stays OPEN for the encryption, and this increment does not touch it. No other `src/` or `include/` path writes key material: the remaining `std::ofstream` sites in `src/main.cpp` are `chain-export --out` (`:3439`, ledger JSON), `snapshot-fetch --out` (`:4812`, a DSN1 snapshot), the three genesis `.hash` companions (`:5517`, `:5795`, `:5833`) and the `ct-timing-probe` CSV (`:16692`), and outside `main.cpp` they are `src/node/node.cpp:126`, `:5148`, `src/chain/chain.cpp:3348` and `src/chain/genesis.cpp:715` — chain, config and snapshot state, none of it secret. Verified by reading each, not by pattern. **(3) Secret material that reaches a shell history rather than a file, unfixed in this binary.** `determ send_anon`, `submit-param-change`, `submit-merge-event`, `submit-dapp-register`, `submit-dapp-call` and `account address` all take the 32-byte seed as a hex ARGV argument (`src/main.cpp:6195`, `:6276`, `:6409`, `:6491`, `:6620`, `:6170`), so it lands in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and in the shell history file. That is the S-110 class, which was closed for `determ-light` only; the daemon has no `--*-seed-from` equivalent. Out of scope here and named so it is not silently dropped. **(4) The key is never zeroized in this command.** `cmd_account_create` holds it in `priv_hex` (`src/main.cpp:6053`), in the `nlohmann::json` object built from it, and in the `std::string` handed to the writer; none is wiped, and `src/crypto/keys.cpp`'s `blob` has the same problem (already recorded 2026-09-17). Wiping needs the JSON path replaced, which is the D2 keyfile work. **(5) The THIRD hand-rolled restricted-write loop.** `wallet/main.cpp::write_bytes_file_0600` and `src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key` are the other two, and they had already drifted from each other on the `write() == 0` case within a day of being written. This increment chose to write the third rather than extract a shared primitive, and says so rather than hiding it: extracting one into `include/determ/` and migrating only these two call sites would leave a header with one consumer and three shapes still in the tree, so the useful version of that change migrates all three — it spans three binaries and two other tracks' files in this wave. Named follow-up: `include/determ/util/restricted_write.hpp` plus all three call sites, as one increment after this wave integrates. **(6) The strace-ordering parser is now in three copies** (`tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg C, `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` leg A, `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` leg B), with the same drift risk; the three are currently in agreement, including on counting both mode-setting spellings. **(7) `O_NOFOLLOW` protects the FINAL path component only.** An attacker who controls a parent directory of `--out` can still redirect the write; the same is true of the two sibling writers, and defending it needs an `O_PATH` directory walk. Not this increment. **(8) `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg A has no skip arm of its own,** so on Windows that wrapper is now RED rather than falsely green. Each of M1..M6 RED against the REBUILT binary on the leg named above, with the marker verified present in that binary, and the source restored and rebuilt clean afterwards.
