## 2026-09-17 — the two S-109 follow-ups: the per-record bulk-import loop, and an atomic publish that published a world-readable file

**Status:** LANDED. Closes the two `wallet/main.cpp` sites S-109 named as its follow-ups. S-109 stays **⚠ OPEN**: Windows is untouched, and the independent permission sites the row names are untouched.

**Problem this change solves — 1: `account-import-many` put every imported account's private seed on disk world-readable, once per record.** It is the bulk-onboarding command — its own header names a 50,000-account custodial migration — and it was the last wallet site writing PLAINTEXT key material on the pre-2026-09-17 shape: `std::ofstream` → write → `std::filesystem::permissions` → `(void)perm_ec`, inside the per-record loop. Reproduced before anything was changed, from a binary rebuilt at the parent commit; plain successful run, `umask 022`, nothing injected and nothing mutated. Under `strace`, for record **2** (not the first, and its target already on disk at 0644):

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../rec2.keyfile", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666) = 3
write(3, "DAK1KK\320\254\3354\213\374\3532\314\213\243\2432\236\225\322\226\0`IP\233a;\324\315"..., 68) = 68
fchmodat(AT_FDCWD, ".../rec2.keyfile", 0600) = 0
```

and bytes 36..68 of that file are **byte-equal** to that record's `privkey_hex`. Measured a second way, with a passive `LD_PRELOAD` observer that forwards every call to libc unchanged and only records the state of the file at the instant the narrowing is attempted:

```
FCHMODAT .../rec1.keyfile want=0600 was=0644 size=68
FCHMODAT .../rec2.keyfile want=0600 was=0644 size=68
FCHMODAT .../rec3.keyfile want=0600 was=0644 size=68
```

`was=0644 size=68` — world-readable AND already holding the complete container, for **every** record. That matters: a gate that only inspects the first record leaves every later iteration ungated, and at N=50,000 the window opens 50,000 times. The P-2 half was live here too: under a shim returning EPERM from every chmod/fchmod/fchmodat, the command left three 0644 key files, exited **0**, wrote **zero bytes** to stderr and recorded `"status": "ok"` for each.

**Problem 2: `keyfile-rotate` did the atomic-publish dance correctly and published a world-readable file anyway.** It stages to `<out>_tmp.bin`, `fsync`s, and `fs::rename`s over the target — but the staging file was created by `std::ofstream` at the umask mode and narrowed only AFTER the rename. **The mode travels with the inode**, so the wide file existed under the FINAL name and the narrowing that follows closes a window already published through. Measured with the same observer wrapping `rename(2)` and reading the destination's mode the instant the call returns, on a `--out` that pre-existed at 0644:

```
RENAME <tmp> -> <out> srcmode=0644 size=171 rc=0 destmode_after=0644
FCHMODAT <out>        want=0600 was=0644 size=171
```

The staging file is always newly created, so there is no "only on overwrite" escape: this one is unconditional. The content is AEAD-wrapped (DNK1 + DWE2), so its severity sits below the plaintext sites, but it was the one write-and-rename shape in the file and the ordering defect was intact. Its P-2 half was live as well: with narrowing denied the rotation left a 0644 keyfile, printed nothing and reported `"rotated": true`.

**The change.** Both sites are routed through the file's existing restricted-write primitive, `write_bytes_file_0600` — `::open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600)` AND `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` before the first write, both required because the create mode applies only when the file is created. **No second or third copy of that primitive was written**, which is the specific thing the wave's lesson 17 asks about; nothing here is streamed, so an open-restricted-then-stream writer would have been a new primitive for no gain. The helper gained exactly one parameter, `std::string* err_out`, defaulting to `nullptr`: when non-null the HARD-FAILURE reason goes there instead of stderr. That exists for one reason — `account-import-many` is a fault-tolerant loop whose documented contract is to put a failure in THAT record's summary entry and keep importing, and a stderr-only diagnostic loses the per-record attribution at N=50k. The open / `fchmod` / write / narrow sequence and every guarantee are identical either way; the other eleven callers pass `nullptr` and are byte-for-byte unchanged. The P-2 **warning** still goes to stderr whatever `err_out` says: it describes a file that WAS written and that the operator must go and fix by hand.

For `account-import-many`, both the encrypted and the plaintext branch call the helper per record, and the zeroization stayed exactly where it was — `determ_secure_zero(bytes.data(), …)` immediately after the call, inside the same iteration — because each record is its own file and its buffer must not outlive the iteration that produced it. A record whose keyfile could not be narrowed carries a failure-only `"perms_narrowed": false`, so a fully successful summary is byte-identical to the old shape and the determinism comparison in `tools/test_wallet_account_import_many.sh` keeps holding.

For `keyfile-rotate`, the staging write goes through the helper and the fsync and the atomic rename that follow are untouched — they are the reason that site was otherwise the best-shaped writer in the file. The helper does NOT fsync and was deliberately not taught to: pushing an fsync into a primitive eleven other callers share is a rider. The post-rename `permissions()` call is kept — belt-and-braces on POSIX, the ONLY narrowing on Windows — and its `error_code` is now CHECKED, feeding the same `perms_narrowed` field.

**The gate.** `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` was **EXTENDED, not duplicated**: it already owned this surface and already carried the ordering leg and the EPERM-shim leg for this binary, and it is already in the FAST `ONLY_PATTERN`, so the FAST total is unchanged. **18 → 44 assertions, 0 sections skipped** on this box, 3.7 s.

New section C, under `strace`, runs against **PRE-EXISTING 0644 targets** for both sites, because `open(O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0600)` applies its mode only when it creates the file — a fresh-create test cannot tell a create-mode-only fix from a correct one. For `account-import-many` it asserts records **2 and 3**, so a fix that restricts only the first file of the loop goes RED. For `keyfile-rotate` the subject of the assertion is the **staged temp**, because the mode travels with the inode through `rename(2)`: the file published under the final name IS that inode. The property asserted, over the trace, is that among the mode-setting calls affecting the temp between its creating open and the first write to that descriptor at least one EXISTS and the LAST one sets 0600, that nothing between that first write and the rename sets anything but 0600, and that the rename to the final name actually happened — otherwise the first three clauses would describe a file nobody published. Path-based `chmod` / `fchmodat` / `fchmodat2` naming the file count alongside descriptor-based `fchmod`, or a create-0600 → widen-by-path → write → narrow-back mutant reads as closed with the window fully open and satisfies every final-mode assertion in the tree. The leg does NOT assert on the `openat`'s mode argument: `strace` prints that argument whether or not the kernel used it. A parser self-check re-runs the same parse over a trace with the pre-write mode-setting lines removed — **both** spellings stripped — and requires the answer `none`.

Sections B5/B6 add the reporting legs under the shim the wrapper already builds and capability-probes. For `account-import-many` the harm is asserted where it is real: records 2 and 3 are left at **644** while record 1, freshly created, still reaches 0600 from the `open(2)` mode — so the 644 is a statement about the overwrite path and not about a broken create — together with the per-record stderr diagnostic naming a NON-first record and `perms_narrowed: false` on every ok record of the summary. For `keyfile-rotate` the honest assertion is different and is written as such: with every chmod denied the published file is **0600**, because the staging temp is CREATED restricted and the shim cannot touch an `open(2)` mode — at the parent commit this same command left it at **644** with an empty stderr and exit 0, which is the discriminator. Its two diagnostics are distinguished by the PATH they name, fixed-string, so the post-rename one (the `(void)perm_ec` this increment removes) cannot be satisfied by the staging one. Success paths are asserted unchanged in both: 0600, empty stderr, no `perms_narrowed` field anywhere.

**Mutants — each applied ALONE to the verified source, RED against the REBUILT binary, restored and rebuilt clean afterwards.** The harness refuses a verdict unless the mutation text is in the source AND an injected external-linkage marker is in the source AND `cmake --build` exited 0 AND that marker is found by `strings` in the RELINKED binary.

| id | mutation | goes RED on |
|----|----------|-------------|
| M1 | restore the `ofstream` create in `account-import-many` (both branches, narrow after, discard `perm_ec`) | C rec2, C rec3, B5 rec1 mode, B5 stderr, B5 summary field |
| M2 | restore the `ofstream` create of the `keyfile-rotate` staging temp | C rotate ordering, B6 published mode, B6 staging stderr |
| M3 | drop the `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` and keep only the `O_CREAT 0600` mode | section A, C rec2, C rec3, C rotate ordering, B shamir stderr, B5 stderr, B6 staging stderr |
| M4 | in `account-import-many`, restrict only the FIRST record of the loop | C rec2, C rec3, B5 stderr, B5 summary field |
| M5 | in `keyfile-rotate`, go back to discarding the post-rename `error_code` | B6 post-rename stderr |
| M6 | widen the file BY PATH between the restricted create and the first write, narrow again at the end so the final mode is still 0600 | section A, C rec2, C rec3, C rotate ordering |

M3 is the measured lesson restated: it leaves the final mode correct on every fresh create and is caught only by the pre-existing-0644 legs. M6 is the one that kills a descriptor-only parser.

**Riders.** None. The files touched are `wallet/main.cpp`, `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh`, the S-109 row in `docs/SECURITY.md`, one falsified sentence in `docs/proofs/WalletRecoveryFlows.md`, and this entry. No consensus accept rule, apply path, wire format, digest, genesis field or migration; no on-disk format change — DAK1 and DNK1 are byte-identical and every existing keyfile still loads; `tools/run_all.sh` is NOT touched, because the wrapper's stem was already in the FAST alternation.

**One behaviour change that is not a bug fix, stated because the previous wave failed to state its own.** The helper opens with `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a per-record target that is a **symlink** now fails with `ELOOP` where `account-import-many` previously wrote through it. Measured both ways on the same input: at the parent commit a symlink planted in `--out-dir` sent 68 bytes of a customer's plaintext seed to the link's target and that record still reported `"status": "ok"` with exit 0; now the record reports `"status": "error"` with the `ELOOP` reason in its `reason` field and the batch continues. **The command's exit code does not change** — `account-import-many` is per-record fault-tolerant and returns 0 for a record-level failure — so the change is visible in the summary, not in `$?`. `keyfile-rotate`'s staging path gains the same protection; there it is unreachable in practice because the stale temp is unlinked first, and it was measured to be: a symlink planted at `<out>_tmp.bin` is removed, the rotation succeeds and exits 0. Nothing in this increment adds a `throw`, so the wave's lesson 12 has no caller audit to report beyond that.

**What does NOT change, and the decision behind it.** The **six** remaining independent `std::filesystem::permissions` sites in `wallet/main.cpp` that still discard `perm_ec` are deliberately left alone: `account-import-many --summary` (`wallet/main.cpp:2319`) is an address-to-path map, `backup-create --envelopes-out` (`:3223`) is AEAD-wrapped, and `cold-sign` (`:9801`), `sign-anon-tx` (`:10186`), `tx-batch-sign` (`:10803`) and `param-change-build` (`:23566`) write signed transactions whose entire purpose is to be broadcast. Fixing the P-2 REPORTING on all six is mechanical, but it is a rider across six commands and four `--json` contracts on a change whose subject is key material, and this repo's own record — three slashing attempts sunk by bundling — says no. Fixing the P-1 ORDERING on all six is **not** mechanical: all six write through a TEXT-mode `std::ofstream`, while the hardened helper is binary-mode on both branches, so routing them through it would silently change their on-disk bytes on Windows — today `\n` is translated to CRLF on those six files, afterwards it would not be — in files downstream tooling parses, on a platform this branch cannot execute. That is its own increment, with its own gate and its own Windows verification. The two bare `::chmod(out_path, 0600)` audit/history exports (`:19051`, `:19518`) keep their recorded best-effort decision. **Windows is not fixed and nothing here claims it is**: `_S_IREAD|_S_IWRITE` drives only FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY and the effective ACL comes by inheritance from the parent directory (`docs/proofs/S005PassphraseKeyfile.md` F-4), so the Windows branch of the helper keeps the previous `ofstream` behaviour rather than implying a fix. S-109 therefore stays OPEN and its summary cells do not move.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (1) Three wallet outputs narrow **nothing at all** — not even after the fact — and S-109 had not named them before this entry: `create-recovery` writes the DRS1 container of password-wrapped share envelopes with a bare `ofstream` and no permission call (`wallet/main.cpp:6051`), and `encrypt-message` (`:7098`) and `decrypt-message` (`:7264`) write through a SECOND unhardened byte-writer, `write_file_bytes` (`:6917`), which has no permission call either — and `decrypt-message --out` is the recovered PLAINTEXT, which is the whole point of the command. They are named in the S-109 row as of this entry and are not fixed here: each is a different content class with its own `--json` contract, and the increment that fixes them should migrate `write_file_bytes` onto the one primitive rather than add a third. (2) `keyfile-rotate`'s header comment still says the command stages to `<out>_tmp.json` in two places (`wallet/main.cpp:3818` and `:3868`) where the code has used `_tmp.bin` for some time; only the one clause this change falsified — step 10 of the Flow list — was corrected, because the rest is unrelated staleness. (3) When the staging narrowing fails but the post-rename one succeeds, `keyfile-rotate` reports `perms_narrowed: false` over a file that is in fact 0600. That is the helper's existing semantics for its other eleven callers — the two failures are OR-ed — and it errs toward telling the operator to check; making it observational would mean `stat`ing the result, which is a different design. (4) `account-import-many` per-record failures still write nothing to stderr, exactly as before; the reason lives in the summary, and an operator who passes no `--summary` sees only the aggregate counts. (5) The `fs::exists(out_path) && !force` precondition remains TOCTOU-racy against the helper's open; `O_NOFOLLOW` removes the symlink flavour of that race but not the general one. (6) A failed write still leaves a truncated or empty file behind, because `O_TRUNC` runs before it — unchanged from the previous shape, and unlike the node-key case there is no `fs::exists()` provisioning check anywhere that would read the leftover as success.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on **Linux x86_64** — build **7 targets**, **FAST 323 passed / 0 failed**, **16 doc guards green**. The FAST count is unchanged on purpose: an existing wrapper was extended rather than a fourth one added for the same surface. The gate alone, from the worktree root against the freshly built `determ-wallet`: **44 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped sections**; against a binary rebuilt at the parent commit, **10 of those 44 RED**. Mutants M1..M6 each RED against the rebuilt binary, restored and rebuilt clean afterwards, with the restored source's checksum matching the pre-mutation one and the gate green again.

**Authority:** the standing doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` — provable security (B3), new behaviour ships with a falsify-on-mutant gate at the layer where the rule lives, smallest increment that keeps the tree green AND truthful, no riders. The follow-up scope is the one S-109 itself names. No owner decision is required or implied: no recorded decision changes, no format changes, and the judgement calls taken here — leaving the six non-key-material permission sites and the three unnarrowed outputs for their own increments — are stated above and in the S-109 row rather than left to inference. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-17. This entry is append-only per convention and carries no tier marker in its body.

## 2026-09-18 — the suite was swept for gates that cannot fail: four more found and fixed, the sweep made a repeatable gate, and skips finally counted in the summary

**Status:** LANDED. Fixes four wrappers that could report success having verified nothing, adds a self-testing ratchet so the class cannot regrow silently, adds ADDITIVE skip accounting to `tools/run_all.sh`, corrects two stale documentation figures, and hands the next increment a file:line work list for the C++ selftests and for two wrappers that are RED today. **No ledger id is allocated** — see "Ledger" below.

**Problem this change solves.** Three increments landed in the two days before this one whose entire subject was a gate that could not fail: a durability leg invisible on every non-x86 architecture, a key-permission check whose two branches both printed `PASS`, and an integration pass that found a wrapper printing `PASS` when the binary it tests was absent. Each was found BY ACCIDENT, one at a time, by a reviewer looking at something else. Nobody had swept the suite. A previous reviewer's block-structure detector (`/root/audit/outbox-arm/review/sweep2.py`) reported zero remaining shell `if`/`case` blocks in which every arm passes — a true result, and a FLOOR rather than a ceiling: by its author's own statement it saw only `if`/`case` structure in `tools/*.sh`, and did not see terminal verdict logic, skip accounting, or anything inside an embedded heredoc.

**What was swept, and what was found.** All **731** `tools/*.sh` (of which **570** are `tools/test_*.sh` wrappers; **324** are FAST members), plus — READ-ONLY — the in-process `test-*` blocks of `src/main.cpp`, `wallet/main.cpp` and `light/main.cpp`. Five shapes were searched for: a terminal verdict on `fail_count == 0` with no floor on the assertions actually made; a `SKIP` arm that banks a pass; a multi-arm `if`/`case` in which every arm passes and none can fail; an assertion inside an embedded python heredoc whose comparison can only ever be true or whose failure is swallowed; and a wrapper that prints a `PASS:` marker and exits 0 when the thing under test is absent. Four live instances were fixed here:

1. `tools/test_wallet_cold_sign.sh:289` — the non-POSIX arm of the output-mode check printed `SKIP:` and then did `pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))`. The same shape as the `shamir-rotate` section 28 defect fixed the day before, in the adjacent file, unnoticed. It now increments `skip_count`.
2. `tools/test_wallet_shamir_rotate.sh:488` — the identical spelling, in the very wrapper whose section 28 was fixed on 2026-09-17; the fix landed on the `if` and left the `case` two hundred lines below it alone.
3. `tools/test_light_keybind_surface.sh:159` and `tools/test_light_resume_monotonicity_guard.sh:70` (the loci AFTER the fix; each previously) printed `SKIP: … (source-light checkout)` followed by a terminal `PASS:` and `exit 0` when the source it guards is absent. **Both are among `ci_local`'s sixteen doc guards**, so this was a hole in the verdict itself, not merely in the full suite. There is no such thing as a "source-light checkout": `light/` is tracked, so an absent target is a broken tree, not a platform. Both now fail closed.
4. `tools/test_light_negative_footing.sh:74` and `tools/test_light_wait_surface.sh:233` (again the post-fix loci) — the same bail-out over a tracked source, in two wrappers outside `ci_local`. Both now fail closed; `test_light_negative_footing.sh` additionally gained the `pass_count == 0` floor, since its live leg declines on every box.

Both `tools/test_wallet_cold_sign.sh` and `tools/test_wallet_shamir_rotate.sh` also gained the assertion floor: their verdict was `fail_count == 0` alone, so a box on which every section declined would have printed `PASS` at `0 pass / 0 fail`.

**The convention, written down once.** `tools/common.sh` now carries THE SKIP CONVENTION in full, with the three spellings the repo was simultaneously using on 2026-09-17 named as the reason: a declined check prints `SKIP: ` and names the cause, never touches `pass_count`, is reported next to it, and `pass_count == 0` is a hard FAIL. A binary the wrapper needs, absent, is a FAILURE and not a skip. `dt_skip` is the shared implementation; the eight wrappers with their own `skip()` keep it, since it is this shape.

**Skip accounting in the suite summary — REPORTED, NOT GATED.** `tools/run_all.sh` now prints, next to `RUN` / `PASS` / `FAIL`, how many of the PASSING wrappers declined at least one section and which, and how many of those printed no assertion-level `PASS:` line at all — i.e. banked green having checked nothing. **No verdict and no exit code changes**, deliberately: two sibling tracks are adding gates against the current semantics in this same wave, and the FAST count is a number many documents cite. Turning a skip into a failure means, in order: giving every one of the 161 wrappers whose verdict is still `fail_count == 0` an assertion floor, then deciding per wrapper whether a declined section is a platform (report) or a missing tool (fail), then re-tiering whatever goes red. That is a suite-wide migration and it is not this increment. The runner also now falsifies its own arithmetic before reporting — `PASS + FAIL == RUN`, `SKIP <= PASS`, asserted-nothing `<= SKIP` — because a summary a reader cannot verify is the same defect class as a gate that cannot fail.

**The gate.** `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh` (FAST member; shell + python, no `determ` binary, offline, never skips). **28 assertions** in five legs. **A** drives the REAL `tools/run_all.sh` over five synthetic wrappers in a throwaway tree — clean, declining, declining-and-asserting-nothing, failing, markerless — and pins every column and the exit code. **B** four mutants of that accounting, each of which must turn A RED. **C** a positive control: deleting the one `SKIP:` line from a fixture moves the column 2 → 1 and moves no verdict. **D** the ratchet over the real `tools/*.sh`: D1 no `if`/`case` in which every arm banks a pass and none can fail (zero), D2 no `SKIP` that banks a pass in the same statement (zero), D3 an EXACT allowlist of the five wrappers that still print `PASS:` and exit 0 on a cannot-run guard — so a sixth is RED and a fixed one must be struck off — and D4 zero python heredocs inside a `tools/test_*.sh` gate carrying an always-true comparison or a bare `except: pass`. **E** an inline SELFTEST on every invocation: the checkers are fed the two 2026-09-17 defects verbatim and both heredoc shapes and must flag each; the corrected shapes, and must flag none; and a WRONG-but-falsifiable predicate, which they must NOT flag.

**What the checker can and cannot see.** It can see structure: which branches bank a pass, which bank a failure, whether a bail-out precedes the assertions, whether a heredoc comparison has two identical operands or a bare `except: pass`. It CANNOT see (and the file says so, because the alternative is a guard that lies): (i) a WRONG PREDICATE — both remaining holes of 2026-09-17 were assertions that ran, could fail, and tested the wrong thing, and nothing structural separates those from correct ones; measured, the checkers return zero on `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` as it stood at `a152664`; (ii) embedded awk, perl or sed, and the 37 single-quoted `python -c` one-liners — D4 parses python heredocs only; (iii) a leg that is falsifiable but has never executed anywhere, e.g. the Darwin/BSD arms of several mode assertions; (iv) any C++ selftest; (v) the 161 wrappers (18 of them FAST members) whose verdict is still `fail_count == 0` with no assertion floor — surfaced per run by the new summary columns rather than gated.

**Mutants.** Each planted ONE AT A TIME into a REAL wrapper in the worktree; the harness (`/root/audit/x3/mutants.sh`) REFUSES to report a verdict unless it has confirmed by grepping an injected marker that the mutation reached the file on disk, and re-runs the gate after every restore. M1 both arms of the `cold-sign` mode check bank a pass → D1 RED. M2 the `shamir-rotate` skip arm banks a pass again → D2 RED. M3 `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` prints `PASS:` and exits 0 on a missing binary → D3 RED. M4 an always-true comparison inside `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh`'s trace-parsing heredoc → D4 RED. M5 a bare `except: pass` in the same heredoc → D4 RED. M6, the harness's own falsification, writes its mutation to a file the harness does not grep: **REFUSED, no verdict taken**. M7 removes the floor restored in (1): the repo gate stays GREEN by design (D does not ratchet that shape) and the audit-dir sweep reports it — recorded so the boundary is a decision on the record, not an unnoticed hole. Leg B's four mutants of `run_all.sh`'s own arithmetic use the same marker refusal. Negative direction, run in the same harness: with the tree restored, D1–D4 are all GREEN and the corrected skip arm at `tools/test_wallet_cold_sign.sh:289` is flagged by none of them.

**The detector was falsified before it was trusted.** The sweep tool is `/root/audit/x3/detect_cantfail.py`; the fixture is `/root/audit/x3/fixture/` (one planted instance of each of eleven shapes plus six correct controls — four shell, two C++) and the transcript is `/root/audit/x3/selftest_detector.log`, 18/18. Running it found TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THE DETECTOR, both of which had made it report zero on every tree it had ever been run over: its C1 check searched FORWARD from the end of a helper's signature for an opening brace and so analysed the NEXT function's body; and its H4 check required `not can_raise` while `can_raise` was set true by the very `.exit()` call H4's own precondition demands, so H4 could not fire on any input. A third defect was found by the mutant harness rather than the fixture: D3 required `exit 0` on a line of its own, so `exit 0  # comment` was invisible, and mutant M3 stayed GREEN until that was relaxed. This is the whole point of the increment: a detector nobody has falsified is worth nothing, and two of this one's five checks were silently dead.

**Reported, NOT fixed — the C++ selftests.** `src/main.cpp`, `wallet/main.cpp` and `light/main.cpp` belong to other tracks this wave. Swept read-only; every instance, with the locus:
- `src/main.cpp:22618-22628` — `test-node-key-perms`, the `#ifdef _WIN32` arm prints `SKIP: POSIX file modes do not exist here…` and then the terminal `PASS: node-key-perms all assertions` and returns 0. `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` greps that terminal marker, so on Windows the gate scores GREEN having asserted nothing. The comment immediately above it, at `src/main.cpp:22614`, claims "No pass is banked on a branch that checked nothing (wave doctrine rule 5)" — the terminal marker IS the pass the wrapper banks, so the comment is false as well as the behaviour. This is the platform-skip instance.
- `src/main.cpp:22557` — `check(compute_result == compute_result, "compute_abort_hash deterministic (re-check)")`: tautological, can never fail.
- `src/main.cpp:22559` — `check(chain_result == chain_result, "chain_abort_hash deterministic (re-check)")`: the same. The comment above both, at `src/main.cpp:22550-22556`, says the intent was to check the two hashes DIFFER ("a sanity check that they're not just aliases"); as written neither determinism nor distinctness is asserted.
- Reviewed and NOT defects, listed so the next increment does not re-litigate them: `src/main.cpp:25382`, `:33239` and `:33633` are `check(true, …)` in the house idiom — reaching the line is the assertion and the failure mode is a crash, hang or throw, with a falsifiable sibling assertion beside each.
- `wallet/main.cpp` (5 `test-*` blocks, 3 `check(` calls) and `light/main.cpp` (13 blocks, 49 calls) produced NO findings of any shape.

**Two wrappers are RED at this commit, and were RED before it.** Both are outside FAST and outside `ci_local`'s sixteen guards, so `ci_local` is green with them red; both only became visible because fixing their vacuous bail-outs made them actually run here. `tools/test_light_wait_surface.sh` reports `committee_bound_state_root: opens=14 good=0 bad=14` and `helper calls: opens=8 good=4 bad=4` — its own text calls that an S-042 head-read REGRESSION. `tools/test_light_negative_footing.sh` reports 9 `daemon_asserted` footings where its contract expects 7, and 12 emissions where it expects 10. Either `light/` drifted from the contract or the contracts drifted from `light/`; adjudicating that requires reading `light/`, which belongs to another track this wave, and correcting either side would change what those assertions MEAN, which this increment is scoped not to do. Handed over as the first thing to look at.

**Documentation.** `docs/SECURITY.md` described the FAST tier as "299 wrappers" in two places (§6 prose and the option-1 row of the unit-test table); it was 299 in 2026-08 and the figure had never moved. Both now read **324**, DERIVED and stated as derived: the `ONLY_PATTERN` alternation in `tools/run_all.sh` carries 325 stems, one of which (`dsso_assertion`) has no wrapper file, and the pattern matches 324 of the 570 `tools/test_*.sh` on disk. `docs/proofs/WalletRecoveryFlows.md`'s regression-script table carried six assertion counts that were each between 10 and 30 short (`shamir-rotate` 33 → 52, `keyfile-recover` "30+" → 60, `account-recover` 32 → 57, `account-import` 26 → 58, `keyfile-decrypt` unstated → 52, `keyfile-info` unstated → 40); each is now the number the wrapper printed when run on Linux x86_64 on 2026-09-18, and each says so. Checked and deliberately NOT changed: every other FAST or assertion count in the tree (`CLAUDE.md:14`, `:293`, `:342`; `docs/proofs/AbortDigestCanonicalizationSoundness.md:154`; `docs/proofs/ProofClaimGateTraceability.md:828`; `docs/proofs/BoundedReorgDesign.md`, `BoundedReorgSoundness.md`, `ShardTipMergeDesign.md`, `ClockInjectionSeam.md`; `docs/SECURITY.md:1479-1485`) is a commit-anchored past-tense measurement — "FAST was N/0 at <commit>" — which a later count does not falsify. `docs/UNIT-TESTS.md:79` and `docs/SECURITY.md:1237` say "155+ subcommands" where `src/main.cpp` now dispatches 251; a lower bound that is still true, left alone rather than re-derived.

**Ledger.** **S-112 is NOT allocated.** Everything fixed here is a verification-coverage defect — a gate that could report success having verified nothing — and not a defect in shipped behaviour; the 2026-09-17 precedent recorded exactly that class in this log only. The one candidate for a shipped-code id is the `test_light_wait_surface` S-042 finding above, and it is NOT adjudicated: it may equally be guard drift, and opening a ledger row on an unread diagnosis would be worse than leaving the finding named here with its locus.

**Riders.** None. Outside `tools/`, only the two documentation loci above are touched. No source file, no `CMakeLists.txt`, no wire format, no binary.

**What does not change.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no genesis field, no migration, no binary. No assertion anywhere changes what it MEANS — only whether a run that asserted nothing can report success. No pass/fail verdict and no exit code in `tools/run_all.sh` changes, and no wrapper that was green is red because of this change. `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` gets no row: the new wrapper adds no CLI surface, matching `tools/test_cluster_output_discipline.sh` and `tools/test_doc_citation_bounds.sh`.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (1) The 161 wrappers whose terminal verdict is `fail_count == 0` with no assertion floor, 18 of them FAST members — the full list is `/root/audit/x3/findings_all.json`, kind `P1`; giving each a floor is a suite-wide migration and the new summary columns make each instance visible when it actually bites. (2) Five wrappers still print a `PASS:` marker and exit 0 on a cannot-run guard and are pinned in D3's exact allowlist: `tools/test_cluster_output_discipline.sh:174` (a known FALSE POSITIVE of the heuristic — that line is its SELFTEST terminal, and it is listed because the allowlist is the checker's output, not a judgement), `tools/test_light_block_verify.sh:35`, `tools/test_light_fetch_validators.sh:26`, `tools/test_light_verify_chain_file.sh:35` and `tools/test_light_verify_unstake_eligibility.sh:155`. Each bails on an absent BINARY or an absent multi-node cluster, which is an environment rather than a broken tree — unlike the four fixed above, which bailed on an absent TRACKED SOURCE. (3) Seven `tools/operator_*.sh` heredocs carry a bare `except: pass`: `tools/operator_anon_address_usage.sh:551` and `:552`, `tools/operator_dapp_topic_audit.sh:179`, `tools/operator_genesis_inspect.sh:259`, `tools/operator_peer_topology.sh:297`, `tools/operator_rpc_auth_probe.sh:278`, `tools/operator_rpc_method_surface.sh:306`. These are operator REPORTS, not gates — none produces a suite verdict — so D4 is scoped to `tools/test_*.sh` and they are named here instead. (4) `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh` excludes ITSELF from the D1–D4 sweep, because it carries verbatim copies of the 2026-09-17 defects as leg-E fixtures and would otherwise report its own fixtures as tree defects; leg E is what stands behind it, and its verdict carries the `pass_count` floor. (5) Seven wrappers already used the correct `skip()` shape before this change and were left exactly as they were.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` from the worktree root on Linux x86_64, `-j1`, `CCACHE_DIR=/root/.ccache` — configure + build **7 targets**, **FAST 324 passed / 0 failed** (323 at this branch's base; +1 is `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh`, added to the FAST `ONLY_PATTERN`), **16 doc guards green**. The gate alone: 28 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip. Mutants M1–M5 each RED with the mutation confirmed present in the file, M6 REFUSED as designed, M7 as described, the tree restored and re-verified green after each. Detector self-test 18/18 against the synthetic fixture.

**Authority:** the standing doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` — provable security (B3): no gate without a mutant that turns it RED, green is not proof, smallest increment that keeps the tree green AND truthful. The 2026-09-17 entries above it establish the precedent this one follows: a gate that cannot fail is recorded here and not in the ledger. No owner decision is required or implied; the decision this increment explicitly does NOT take is making a declined section fail the suite, which changes the meaning of the published FAST count and belongs to whoever owns that number. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-18. This entry is append-only per convention and carries no tier marker in its body.

## 2026-09-18 — integration pass over the three gate-and-permissions increments: a FAST gate that went RED on Windows, two counts the merge falsified, and the adjudication of two long-RED wrappers

**Status:** LANDED. Fixes three defects that exist only in the combination of the three increments above, and puts on the record an adjudication that has been outstanding since one of them made two dormant wrappers run again.

**Problem 1 — a FAST gate went RED on Windows, and the increment that did it reported the opposite.** The S-111 increment stopped `test-node-key-perms`' Windows arm from banking a pass: it now prints a `SKIP:` marker instead of the terminal `PASS: node-key-perms all assertions` and exits non-zero. That was correct. But `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg A greps for exactly that PASS marker and had no way to read a SKIP, so it scored a FAIL — and that wrapper is a FAST member, while `.github/workflows/ci.yml` carries a `windows-2022` job running `bash tools/ci_local.sh`. The increment's own report says "On Linux (this box and CI) nothing changes"; the CI matrix is not Linux-only, and `tools/ci_local.sh`'s own header calls the MSVC/Windows box the primary one. Leg A now records the platform SKIP by name through `dt_skip`, and the wrapper gained the `pass_count > 0` floor it was missing, so a platform where every section skips fails closed instead of printing PASS. Verified both ways on this box: Linux unchanged at 7 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped, and with the in-process arm forced to its skip path leg A records `SKIP: section A …` rather than a failure.

**Stated with it, because it is worse than what this wave broke:** `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` — also a FAST member — **was already RED on Windows before this wave**. Both of its sections are Linux/`LD_PRELOAD`-gated and it carries a `pass_count == 0` floor, so on `windows-2022` it exits 1. That is not a defect introduced here and it is not fixed here; it means the Windows job has been failing since that gate landed, and nobody noticed, which is its own finding. Whoever next owns `tools/` should give both wrappers' remaining legs named skips, or the Windows job an explicit expectation.

**Problem 2 — the merge manufactured a false measurement.** `docs/proofs/WalletRecoveryFlows.md` records `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` as "18 assertions (measured 2026-09-18 on Linux x86_64 — this one was already right) … Both legs SKIP by name". The measurement was honest when taken: the sweep increment measured the wrapper, and the wallet increment then extended that same wrapper from 18 to 44 assertions and from two sections to three, in the same wave, in a file the sweep did not touch again. Neither track could see it. Corrected to 44 in three sections, with the reason recorded in the row rather than a second bare number. This is the defect class the sweep increment exists to remove, produced by the integration of that very increment, which is worth saying plainly.

**Problem 3 — my own integration edit left a stale denominator.** Correcting the FAST count to **325** (two tracks each added one wrapper to a base of 323) left the sentence reading "matches 325 of the **570** `tools/test_*.sh` on disk"; there are **571**, the S-111 increment having added one. The sentence advertises itself as DERIVED. None of the sixteen doc guards derives that count, so nothing would have caught it. Both numbers are now measured against the tree as it stands.

**The adjudication that was outstanding: two long-RED wrappers are GUARD DRIFT, not a regression in `light/`.** The sweep increment fixed four wrappers that had been bailing out vacuously, and two of them then ran for the first time in a long while and came up RED — `tools/test_light_wait_surface.sh`, whose own text calls its finding an "S-042 head-read REGRESSION" (`committee_bound_state_root: opens=14 good=0 bad=14`), and `tools/test_light_negative_footing.sh` (9 `daemon_asserted` footings against a hard-coded 7, 12 emissions against 10). Both are outside FAST and outside the sixteen guards, so `ci_local` is green with them red. **Adjudicated by re-running each wrapper's own extraction against `light/`: there is no regression.** The wait-surface guard requires the wait variable to be the LAST argument of the call it inspects; all fourteen "bad" call sites do forward it, and `light/trustless_read.hpp`'s signature gained `expected_k` and `bft_enabled` AFTER the guard was written, so the wait argument is simply no longer last. The negative-footing guard's substantive legs all pass — `ungated=0`, `mismatched=0`, correctly gated and correctly labelled — and exactly three assertions fail, every one a hard-coded census pin that was never updated when two commands gained correctly-gated footings. **No S-row is opened**: nothing in the shipped client is wrong. Repairing the two contracts changes what those assertions MEAN, which is its own increment with its own review, and it is the next thing worth doing in `tools/`. Not established without a cluster: whether the two new footings are the semantically right class, and the live behavioural leg.

**Corrections this append-only log owes itself.** (a) The sweep increment's entry says the FAST tier is now **324** and that both `docs/SECURITY.md` sentences "now read 324"; integrated with the S-111 increment the count is **325**, the alternation carries **326** stems, and there are **571** wrappers on disk. All four figures in that sentence are superseded; the two documentation sentences read 325 as of this entry. (b) The wallet increment's entry is dated **2026-09-17** and sits between two 2026-09-18 entries; its commit is dated 2026-09-18 and the log's order is otherwise monotone. (c) The S-111 increment's new gate asserts `RC == 0` on the unprotectable-file path, which PINS the residual it documents — a future increment that makes that path refuse must edit the gate, not only the code.

## 2026-09-18 — the macOS run was RED on one wrapper, and it was the gate's fault: a Linux-only gate now asserts the outcome everywhere POSIX modes exist

**Status:** LANDED. Fixes a gate that could not run on the owner's own third platform, found by the owner running it.

**Problem.** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Darwin arm64 came back **RUN 325 / PASS 324 / FAIL 1**, the one failure being `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh`: `0 pass / 0 fail / 3 skipped section(s)` → `FAIL: every section skipped; nothing was asserted`. All three of its sections need Linux — two need `strace`, one needs `LD_PRELOAD` to intercept `chmod` (SIP blocks that on macOS) — so on Darwin the wrapper declined everything and the `pass_count > 0` floor, added the day before precisely so a run that asserted nothing could not report success, correctly called that a failure. **The floor is right and the wrapper was wrong.** A gate that cannot observe its property on a platform must not claim the product is broken there; and the entry above this one predicted exactly this for the `windows-2022` CI job, named it as pre-existing, and did not draw the obvious conclusion that macOS is in the same position. The owner's run drew it.

**What was actually missing: the outcome is observable on macOS; only the window is not.** `stat` works there and POSIX modes exist. What needs `strace` is the ORDER (was the file 0600 before the secret was written) and what needs `LD_PRELOAD` is the REPORTING of a failed narrowing. The mode each output ends at — the contract `write_bytes_file_0600` states — is observable on every POSIX platform, and the wrapper was not asserting it anywhere.

**The change.** A fourth section, D, gated on `uname` for the POSIX family and needing neither strace nor a compiler. It asserts the final mode of six outputs across the four commands this wrapper covers: a fresh `shamir-split --out`; `shamir-rotate` over a PRE-EXISTING 0644 target; **each of the three records** of `account-import-many`, since the defect that increment fixed was per-record and a fix that restricts only the first must fail; and the atomically published `keyfile-rotate` target, also over a pre-existing 0644 file. The terminal line now reports how many assertions were checked and how many sections declined, and says in the wrapper's own output that what declined is not asserted.

**What section D does NOT gate, written into the section so a green is not misread.** It asserts the outcome and not the window, and not the reporting. A mutant that restores the old create-then-narrow shape leaves the final mode 0600 and is GREEN in section D — which is why sections A, B and C exist and why this one does not replace them. On a platform without strace this gate now covers the contract, not the window S-109 was opened for. That distinction is the whole reason the S-109 window was invisible to every after-the-fact check in the first place, and it would be dishonest to let a Darwin green read as more than it is.

**Falsified before it was trusted.** Mutant D1 — the helper's trailing narrowing widened to 0644 — rebuilt, run with `strace` and the C compiler hidden so section D was the only judge: **five of the six assertions RED**, `1 pass / 5 fail`. The one that stayed green is `keyfile-rotate`, whose post-rename narrowing is its own call site rather than the helper's, which is evidence the six assertions are six properties and not one property in six sets of clothes. Source restored and rebuilt clean; the harness refused a verdict on an earlier attempt whose anchor no longer matched the file, rather than reporting a green mutant.

**The ratchet caught my own first attempt at this, and I fixed the wrapper rather than the gate.** My initial summary branched — `if skip_count > 0` print one PASS line `else` print another — and `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh` D1 went RED on it: `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh:641 | if [ "$skip_count" -gt 0 ]`, an if/case in which every arm banks a pass and no arm can fail. The intent was to vary the wording of the terminal marker, not to make a verdict, but the shape is indistinguishable from the defect the ratchet exists to forbid, and a rule that is kept and then special-cased for its author is worthless. The summary is now one unconditional terminal marker carrying both counts. This is the ratchet doing on new code, the day after it landed, exactly what it was built for.

**What is still RED, and where.** On **Windows** this wrapper remains red: there is no POSIX mode to assert, so section D declines there too and the wrapper has nothing left. That is not fixable inside this file — the property genuinely does not exist on that platform, and the honest outcome is a wrapper-level SKIP, which `tools/run_all.sh` has no notion of: its per-wrapper outcome is PASS or FAIL, a missing marker counts as FAIL, and its self-checked arithmetic asserts `PASS + FAIL == RUN`. Adding a third outcome means changing that invariant and the "FAST N passed" figure many documents cite, which is a deliberate repo-wide change and not a rider on a macOS fix. `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` is in the same position on Windows. Both are named here as the next increment in `tools/`, with the design: a third outcome, counted separately, with the arithmetic invariant widened to `PASS + FAIL + SKIPPED == RUN` and the suite still exiting non-zero only on FAIL.

**What does not change.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no migration, and no C++ source at all: this entry changes one test wrapper. No triage row opens, closes or changes status; no summary cell moves. FAST stays at 325 wrappers.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, FAST 325 passed / 0 failed, 16 doc guards green; `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` 50 assertions on Linux and 6 with strace and the compiler hidden, both green, and 1 pass / 5 fail under mutant D1 in the second configuration.

**Authority:** the standing verification doctrine in `CLAUDE.md`. The defect was reported by the owner's own Darwin arm64 run of `tools/ci_local.sh`, which is the second-platform gate working as designed. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-18. This entry is append-only per convention and carries no tier marker in its body.

## 2026-09-18 — three hand-rolled restricted writers had drifted twice in two days; they become ONE primitive, every deliberate divergence stays a parameter, and the one divergence that was drift is fixed and gated

**Status:** LANDED. One new header (`include/determ/util/restricted_write.hpp`), three call sites migrated (`wallet/main.cpp::write_bytes_file_0600`, `src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key`, `src/main.cpp::write_account_file_0600`), four assertions added to an existing in-process selftest. **No new FAST wrapper and no `tools/` file touched** — the FAST count is unchanged. No consensus, apply, wire, digest, genesis or state surface; no migration; no new dependency; no CLI flag; no exit-code change anywhere.

**Problem this change solves.** Three implementations of "put a secret on disk in a file that is 0600 before its first byte" were written independently on 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18 by three different agents, and they drifted **twice inside those two days, measurably**. First: two of them disagreed on `write() == 0` — the wallet's guarded it, `save_node_key`'s would have spun forever — caught by review and fixed on 2026-09-18. Second, and still live at this branch's base: **only the wallet writer omitted `::unlink` on the write- and close-failure paths**, so a truncated key container survived under the final name, where `src/crypto/keys.cpp` removes it and says why at the locus ("never leave a partial identity behind", "the contents are not trustworthy") and `src/main.cpp` removes it and says why ("what is on disk is a FRAGMENT of a private key under a name an operator reads as a provisioned account"). The third copy was written **deliberately**, and its own entry (2026-09-18, `account create --out`) says so and names this extraction as the follow-up: *"Named follow-up: `include/determ/util/restricted_write.hpp` plus all three call sites, as one increment after this wave integrates."* This is that increment.

**The wallet defect, REPRODUCED against the binary built from HEAD before anything was touched** (transcript in the session's audit directory). An `LD_PRELOAD` shim that makes `write(2)` return 0 for every descriptor above stderr — the condition the guard in all three writers exists for, and one the kernel will not produce on a regular file:

```
$ LD_PRELOAD=zerowrite.so determ-wallet shamir-split --secret <32 hex> --threshold 2 --shares 3 --out $T/s.json
shamir-split: write failed: /tmp/.../s.json: wrote 0 bytes
rc=1
$ stat -c '%a %s %n' $T/s.json
600 0 /tmp/.../s.json
$ LD_PRELOAD=zerowrite.so determ-wallet account-import --priv <32 hex> --out $T/k.dak1
account-import: write failed: /tmp/.../k.dak1: wrote 0 bytes
rc=1
600 0 /tmp/.../k.dak1
```

The command exits 1 and says so, and a **zero-byte key container survives under the final name** — which the `--force` guard on the next attempt then refuses to overwrite. The same probe against the daemon (`account create --out`) and against `save_node_key` (`determ init`) leaves nothing behind, because those two already unlink.

**The difference table, which is the durable part of this increment.** Before a line of the primitive was written, every behavioural difference between the three was enumerated and each one classified as POLICY (a deliberate choice of that call site, which the primitive must keep parameterised) or DRIFT (three copies disagreeing for no stated reason, which the primitive resolves). The full table is in the session's audit directory; its conclusions:

*Identical in all three, so the primitive simply owns them:* the open flags and create mode (`O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW`, `0600`); `O_NOFOLLOW`; `::fchmod(fd, 0600)` on the descriptor before the first byte; EINTR (three spellings, one semantics); short writes; the refusal to spin on `write() == 0`; a checked `::close`; and the absence of an `fsync` — `keyfile-rotate` re-opens and fsyncs its staging file itself "rather than pushing an fsync into a primitive ten other callers share", and that recorded reason now applies to the shared primitive verbatim.

*POLICY, kept and parameterised at the call site:* **(1)** what a failed pre-write narrowing does — the wallet and the daemon warn and CONTINUE (a `keyfile-recover` result may be unregenerable; refusing in the daemon is an exit-code change named as the S-111 remainder), `save_node_key` REFUSES (a node identity is regenerable at no cost and is read for the life of the deployment). `on_narrow_failure = Continue | Refuse`. **(2)** whether the trailing belt-and-braces `std::filesystem::permissions` call happens at all — the wallet and the daemon keep it and CHECK its `error_code`, `save_node_key` has none and deliberately so. `final_narrow`. **(3)** Windows text vs binary mode, which is about ON-DISK BYTES: the wallet switched to binary knowingly and changed its Windows output, and both `src/` sites deliberately did not repeat that. `windows_binary`. **(4)** the reporting shape — stderr with a `<cmd_label>:` prefix plus an optional `err_out` and a `perms_narrowed_out` flag; unprefixed stderr; or a throw. **Every diagnostic string, and every throw, stays at its call site and is byte-identical**; the primitive returns a status and the caller renders it, with the formula `msg + (err ? ": " + strerror(err) : "")` reproducing each site's previous POSIX **and** Windows text verbatim. **(5)** the test-only `DETERM_NODE_KEY_INJECT` hook: the `getenv` and the decision to honour it stay in `src/crypto/keys.cpp` where they were justified; the primitive only carries the errno in, and the other two sites pass 0. **(6)** creating and narrowing the parent DIRECTORY, which only `save_node_key` does and only for a directory it created itself — that stays entirely in `keys.cpp`.

*DRIFT, resolved:* **(a)** the wallet's missing `::unlink` after a failed write or close. The wallet's own comment justifying "the file is NOT deleted" is about the **failed-narrowing** path, where the file is COMPLETE and merely too wide — a good argument, kept unchanged. It says nothing about a failed write, where `O_TRUNC` has already run and what survives is a fragment that every container the wallet writes (DAK1 / DSS1 / DNK1 / DBE1 / DWE2) rejects on its own magic and length checks. Both siblings state the opposite rule at the locus, the wave doctrine's "never leave a file behind on a refusal path" is binding on all three, and the independent review of this wave reached the same verdict. Resolved: the primitive removes the file on every failure path that has already truncated it. **(b)** `save_node_key`'s Windows arm never checked its stream after close (`f << blob;` and the stream destructor swallows a failed flush), so a truncated node identity was reported as a success; both siblings check it, the 2026-09-17 entry's words are "left exactly as it was" rather than "designed", and its Windows reasoning is entirely about `_S_IREAD`/`_S_IWRITE` and NTFS ACLs, i.e. about permissions and not about error checking. The primitive checks it for all three.

**Header-only, and that was checked against `CMakeLists.txt` rather than assumed.** The consumers are two separate `add_executable` targets — `determ` (which compiles both `src/main.cpp` and `src/crypto/keys.cpp`) and `determ-wallet`. The only library between them is `determ-crypto-c99`, whose source list is exclusively `.c` under the C99 / Minix-portable discipline, so a C++ translation unit cannot be added there. Everything in the header is `inline`, and it reaches `determ-wallet` because `determ-crypto-c99` exports `include` as a PUBLIC include directory — which is already how `wallet/main.cpp` includes `<determ/crypto/ed25519/ed25519.h>`.

**The gate.** The three wrappers that pin these three sites — `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` (50 assertions), `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` (7 wrapper over 18 in-process) and `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` (29 wrapper over what were 22 in-process) — are the safety net and **not one line of any of them was edited**; `tools/` belongs to other tracks in this wave. All three stay green with their counts unchanged.

The one behaviour that CHANGED needed its own assertion, and it went where it could go without touching `tools/`: **four new assertions inside `determ test-account-create-perms`** (`src/main.cpp`, 22 to 26), which `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` leg A already runs by grepping its terminal marker. They assert the unified rule directly on the primitive — a write that cannot complete leaves NOTHING behind — against a **real** `::write` failure, produced by lowering `RLIMIT_FSIZE` below the payload with `SIGXFSZ` ignored across the window and the limit restored immediately, and **not** by an injection hook on the shipped write path. A control asserts that the identical call without the limit DOES create the file at 0600, so "absent" is the removal and not a failed open, and a second control asserts the limit really was lowered, so the leg cannot pass vacuously. Because the rule now lives once, in one header compiled into both binaries, that assertion covers all three call sites.

**Mutants — seven, each applied ALONE to the header, REBUILT, then restored and rebuilt clean.** Each injects a unique marker as a function-local `static const char* volatile` (a `const char*` local was discarded by `-O3` for an earlier harness in this project), and the harness REFUSES to report a verdict unless the marker is present in the SOURCE, the build SUCCEEDED, **and** the marker is present in BOTH relinked binaries.

| id | mutation | `test_wallet_out_perms` | `test_node_key_perms` | `test_account_create_perms` | bounded `write()==0` probe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | restore the pre-fix `std::ofstream` create (create at the umask mode, write the secret, narrow afterwards if at all) | **RED** 41/9 | **RED** 3/4 | **RED** 24/5 | spins (an artifact of the ofstream retry loop, not the guard) |
| M2 | keep the 0600 create mode, DROP the `::fchmod` before the write | **RED** 43/7 | **RED** 5/2 | **RED** 25/4 | guarded |
| M3 | `::fchmod` moved to AFTER the write (final mode still 0600) | **RED** 43/7 | **RED** 6/1 | **RED** 25/4 | guarded |
| M4 | create 0600, `fchmod(fd,0600)`, widen the PATH to 0666, write, narrow back by path (final mode 0600) | **RED** 46/4 | **RED** 6/1 | **RED** 27/2 | guarded |
| M5 | remove the `write() == 0` guard | green 50/0 | green 7/0 | green 29/0 | **KILLED** — all three binaries spin and are killed by `timeout`, where the unmutated build exits 1 with each site's own diagnostic |
| M6 | leave the truncated file behind after a failed write (the wallet's pre-2026-09-18 shape) | green 50/0 | green 7/0 | **RED** 28/1 | guarded |
| M7 | leave the empty, `O_TRUNC`'d file behind on a refusal | green 50/0 | **RED** 6/1 | green 29/0 | guarded |

M1..M4 are the window mutants and each is RED on **all three** gates, which is the measured statement that the primitive really is shared: one header edit reddens the wallet, the node key and the daemon at once. M4 is the one that matters most — it ends at mode 0600, so every final-mode assertion in the tree is green on it and only the ordering legs that count path-based calls kill it. M5 is the one **no gate can catch**, by construction: `write(2)` does not return 0 for a positive count on a regular file, so the condition the guard exists for cannot be produced by any of the three gates. The bounded probe produces it with an `LD_PRELOAD` shim that returns 0 for every descriptor above stderr and runs each of the three commands under `timeout 10`: unmutated they exit 1 with `wrote 0 bytes` / `Input/output error` and leave nothing on disk; under M5 all three hang and are killed at 10s. M6 and M7 are the two halves of the one behaviour this increment changed, and each is RED on exactly one gate — M6 on the four new in-process assertions, M7 on `test-node-key-perms`' existing "no file is left behind at all" assertion under `DETERM_NODE_KEY_INJECT=fchmod`. Both of M6's controls stay green, so the kill is specific and not a collapse of the section.

**Riders: none.** No unrelated code improved, no formatting sweep, no other command touched, no new CLI surface, no `tools/` file edited, no FAST wrapper added.

**What does NOT change.** No consensus accept rule, apply path, wire format, digest, genesis field, state layout or migration. No `light/`, `dapps/`, `sim/` or `sdk/` file. Every diagnostic string at every site is byte-identical, verified by the three gates' `grep`-for-exact-text legs. No exit code changes on any path. The on-disk bytes of every output are unchanged on POSIX and on Windows, text-mode translation included — the wallet keeps binary, both `src/` sites keep text. The three reporting policies (warn / warn plus a `--json` flag / throw) are untouched, including `save_node_key`'s refusal and the daemon's deliberate non-refusal. `determ test-node-key-perms` keeps its 18 in-process assertions; `tools/run_all.sh`'s FAST alternation is not touched.

**Ledger: no new S-id, and that is an argument, not an omission.** The wallet's missing `unlink` is a genuine, reproduced, shipped-code defect, and one was reserved for it. It is recorded in `docs/SECURITY.md` as a third mitigation pass on the existing **S-109** row rather than as a row of its own, because: by the time a write can fail the file is already 0600, so no confidentiality boundary is crossed and this is not a permissions exposure; the harm is operational and bounded — exit code 1, a named diagnostic, a per-record `status: error` in the bulk loop, and a fragment every decoder rejects; `keyfile-rotate`, the one site that could publish it, already removed its own staging file; and the defect is CLOSED by the same commit that reports it, so a new row would be opened and closed in one change while moving two summary cells for something no reader ever sees as open. The precedent in this same wave is the `write() == 0` divergence — same three writers, same class, same severity profile — which was recorded in this log and not given an id. Summary cells therefore do not move and `tools/test_security_ledger_coherence.sh` is green.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** **(1)** The Windows close check in **(b)** above is the one change in this increment with **no mutant**: it is unobservable on every platform this box can run a gate on, all three gates SKIP by name on Windows, and it changes no passing path (a close that succeeds behaves identically). It is stated here rather than buried; the alternative — a `check_close` policy field defaulting to true with `keys.cpp` passing false — was rejected because re-encoding an un-argued accident as a parameter of the shared primitive is exactly what this increment exists to stop. **(2)** `::unlink(path)` after a failed write re-resolves the name, so an attacker who already has write access to the containing directory could swap in another name between the `close` and the `unlink` and have that removed instead. `unlink(2)` does not follow symlinks, the attacker must already control the directory, and both `src/` sites have had this exact call since 2026-09-17/18; closing it needs an `O_PATH` directory walk, which is the same work item as **(3)**. **(3)** `O_NOFOLLOW` guards the FINAL path component only; an attacker controlling a parent directory of the output can still redirect the write, at all three sites. Already recorded 2026-09-18; unchanged. **(4)** The **strace-ordering parser is still in three copies** (`tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` leg C, `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` leg A, `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` leg B), with the same drift risk this increment removed from the product code. They are currently in agreement, including on counting both mode-setting spellings. `tools/` is another track's in this wave, so unifying them is not this increment — and it is the next instance of the pattern this entry is about. **(5)** Six independent `std::filesystem::permissions` sites and three unnarrowed outputs in `wallet/main.cpp` still do not go through any restricted writer (enumerated with their loci in the S-109 row); routing them through the primitive is now a much smaller change than it was, but it changes their Windows bytes and is a rider across six commands and four `--json` contracts. **(6)** The secret still passes through a `std::string` and an `nlohmann::json` that are not zeroized at `save_node_key` and `cmd_account_create`; the primitive does not zeroize the caller's buffer either, deliberately — the buffer belongs to the caller and two of the three already wipe theirs. Unchanged, and it is the D2 container increment's work. **(7)** `determ init` still creates its data directory at 0755 (recorded 2026-09-17). **(8)** `docs/SECURITY.md` still describes the FAST tier as "299 wrappers" in two places where it is 325; noticed and left alone twice before, and left alone again for the same reason — it is a shared paragraph two tracks may be editing today and it belongs in the integration pass.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, **FAST 325 passed / 0 failed** (325 at this branch's base; this increment adds no wrapper, so the count is unchanged), 16 doc guards green. `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` alone: 50 pass / 0 fail, 0 sections skipped; `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` alone: 7 pass / 0 fail; `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` alone: 29 pass / 0 fail; `determ test-account-create-perms` alone: 26 assertions. Each mutant's verdict was read only after the build was confirmed to succeed AND the marker was confirmed present in both relinked binaries, and the header was restored and rebuilt clean afterwards with a check that neither binary still carries a mutant marker.

**Authority:** the standing verification doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` (provable security B3; assert at the layer where the rule lives; smallest increment that keeps the tree green AND truthful; no riders), the node-/client-local backlog authorized under D19a as item (11) of the 2026-09-16 implementation sequence, and the explicit follow-up named by the 2026-09-18 `account create --out` entry in this log. No consensus decision is touched and none is implied. Recorded by Claude (Cowork session), 2026-09-18. This entry is append-only per convention and carries no tier marker in its body.
