## 2026-09-18 — the secret-source convention leaves light/: eighteen determ-wallet and determ parse sites stop needing the private key on argv, and the primitive that was written twice becomes one header

**Status:** LANDED. Opens and partially mitigates S-114 (`determ-wallet`) and S-115 (the `determ` daemon), promotes `light/seed_source.{hpp,cpp}` to `include/determ/util/secret_source.hpp` behaviour-preservingly, and adds one FAST gate. The raw flags are NOT removed; the class is NOT closed and this entry names every site left.

**The problem, reproduced by EXECUTION before anything was written** (`/root/audit/z2/REPRO-2026-09-18.txt`). A running process's argument vector is world-readable at `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` — measured `-r--r--r-- root:root`, and read there by a process in a different session with no relationship to the child — `ps -o args=` prints the same line to every user on the host, and the operator's interactive shell writes it verbatim into `$HISTFILE` (all three legs executed, not argued from source). A real Ed25519 private key minted by `determ-wallet account-create-batch` was recovered out of `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` of a `determ-wallet account-import --priv <key>` child, and a real keyfile passphrase out of a `determ account create --passphrase <pw>` child; both children were pinned in a deterministic window by making their `--out` a FIFO, so there is no race and no sampling luck. This is S-110 — reproduced and closed for `determ-light` on 2026-09-17 — in the other two binaries, where it had been left unfixed BY NAME: the S-110 entry's "not in scope" paragraph names `determ-wallet keyfile-create --priv` and `determ-wallet account-import --priv` as deliberately deferred. Twelve `determ-wallet` parse sites and six `determ` parse sites were affected. For a private seed, a master seed, a Shamir secret, an RPC HMAC secret or a keyfile passphrase, that argv string IS the secret.

**The change, and it is ADDITIVE.** Each of the eighteen gained a `--<name>-from <file:path|env:NAME|prompt>` twin: `shamir-split --secret-from`, `envelope encrypt/decrypt --password-from`, `account-derive-batch --seed-from`, `account-import --priv-from`, `backup-create --secret-from`, `keyfile-create --priv-from`, `create-recovery --seed-from` and `--password-from`, `recover --password-from`, `message-sign --priv-from`, `rpc-auth --secret-from`; and in the daemon `account create/decrypt --passphrase-from` and the `--priv-from` of `submit-param-change`, `submit-merge-event`, `submit-dapp-register`, `submit-dapp-call`. The raw flags keep working with the same accepted inputs, the same stdout bytes and the same exit codes; they additionally print the named `WARNING[seed-on-command-line]` line to stderr naming the `-from` alternative. Both forms of one secret at once are refused. A missing or empty file, an unset or empty variable, an empty `file:` path or `env:` name, and an unknown scheme are each refused with a named diagnostic and exit 1. The `DETERM_PASSPHRASE` fallback of the daemon's two account subcommands is unchanged and is still consulted last.

**The primitive that had been written twice is now written once.** `include/determ/util/secret_source.hpp` is header-only for the reason `include/determ/util/restricted_write.hpp` records and which was re-checked against `CMakeLists.txt` rather than assumed: `determ`, `determ-wallet` and `determ-light` are three separate `add_executable` targets and the only library between them, `determ-crypto-c99`, takes only `.c` sources. `light/seed_source.cpp` and `wallet/main.cpp::passphrase_from_source` are now forwarders to it. The two pre-existing copies agreed on every diagnostic string, the three source forms and the exit code, and differed on exactly three things — the noun in the diagnostics, the prompt label, and whether the value is whitespace-trimmed. Those three are the `SecretPolicy` fields; everything else is the mechanism. The trim difference is not cosmetic and is now pinned by a mutant: a passphrase may legitimately begin or end with a space, so a `file:` line loses only its trailing CR/LF and `env:`/`prompt` values are taken verbatim, while a hex seed is trimmed at both ends.

**The move is behaviour-preserving, and the proof is that the gate written for the old code is green UNCHANGED.** `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh` was not edited — not one character — and reports the same 28 assertions passed, including its own in-gate reproduction of S-110 and its `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` reads. The mutant that proves the unchanged gate can still fail is **M4b**, which flips `light/seed_source.hpp`'s `SEED_POLICY` binding to PASSPHRASE — the single point both live light entry points share — and turns that gate RED at five assertions. It is M4b and not M4 because **M4 came back GREEN**, and that is recorded below rather than renumbered away.

**The three sources are RANKED, in every surface an operator reads.** The first cut listed `file:<path> | env:<NAME> | prompt` flat in all five new surfaces — the S-114 and S-115 ledger rows, the two new `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` convention rows and the two binaries' top-level usage blocks — while `docs/SECURITY.md`'s own S-110 row, unchanged since 2026-09-17, already said `file:` with restrictive permissions is the strongest of the three because `env:` stays visible in `/proc/<pid>/environ` to the same UID. The ranking existed only in the header's source comment, which an operator never reads. All five surfaces now carry it, plus the thing that was nowhere said: **`SECRET=... determ-wallet account-import --priv-from env:SECRET` puts the secret straight back into the shell history file**, which is one of the three leaks this entry exists to close. `env:` is worth having when the variable comes from a parent process, a CI secret store or a systemd credential — not when it is typed on the command line.

**The unknown-scheme refusal no longer echoes a long specifier.** It printed `unknown private key source '<spec>'` verbatim. The likeliest way to reach it is the typo `--priv-from <the key itself>` — one character from `--priv <key>`, and the two flags now sit next to each other in every usage string. `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` dies with the process; stderr goes into CI logs, ticket attachments, terminal scrollback and `script` transcripts, which do not, so echoing it converts a transient exposure into a stored one. Specifiers of 16 characters or fewer are still echoed verbatim — every refusal any gate greps for is inside that bound, so no shipped diagnostic changed — a longer one with a colon in its first 16 characters keeps the scheme-looking prefix (`fille:<15 chars elided>`, which is what makes a mistyped scheme diagnosable), and a longer one with no colon is not echoed at all (`<64 chars elided>`). B21b and B21c assert it; M10 is RED.

**One stable marker, deliberately.** Every warning in all three binaries prints `WARNING[seed-on-command-line]`, keeping the historical noun even where the material is a passphrase or an HMAC secret. It is the spelling S-110 shipped and `docs/SECURITY.md` documents; a second spelling would mean an operator grepping the documented marker silently misses two binaries. The sentence under the marker names the actual material and the actual flags.

**The gate.** `tools/test_secret_on_argv.sh`, FAST, 102 assertions, four sections. A EQUIVALENCE (14): byte-identical stdout between the two forms on the deterministic commands, and for the randomized ones — which mint a fresh salt, nonce or polynomial, so byte-equality is not available — the artifact the `-from` form produces reconstructs to the SAME secret. The password fixture carries leading, trailing and internal spaces, so a source that trimmed whitespace would produce a container nobody can open. A5/A6 catch that through the `file:` branch; **A5b/A6b catch it through `env:` and `prompt`, which are a DIFFERENT function** — `detail::normalize_value`, one branch over from `normalize_line` — and were unasserted in the first cut, so a mutant trimming in that one function left all 98 assertions green. Review found it on 2026-09-18; M7b is the mutant that now kills it. B SOURCES (45): for EVERY one of the eighteen pairs, a missing `file:` source is refused with a named diagnostic that names that flag and exits 1 — the assertion that proves the flag is parsed and routed at all, because an unwired flag is ignored and the command prints its required-argument error instead — and both forms at once are refused; plus the other source shapes on representatives, and that an unrecognised specifier longer than 16 characters is ELIDED rather than echoed back. C WARNING (38): for every one of the eighteen, the raw flag warns by name and names its twin, the `-from` form does not, and the warning is a WARNING — the raw form still emits its output and exits 0. **D PROCESS TABLE (5), the property itself, read from the kernel and not from a grep of the source**: with `-from` the secret is ABSENT from the running child's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and with the raw flag it is PRESENT there, both children pinned by a FIFO.

**The window is SYNCHRONISED on the kernel, and the first cut of this increment got it wrong.** It polled `/proc/<pid>/comm` until the child had exec'd and then slept 100 ms, and the four documents that described it — the wrapper's header, its own PASS text, the S-115 ledger row and an earlier draft of this entry — all said the sample was taken "strictly AFTER the envelope was sealed". Independent review measured it, 5 runs out of 5: at the sampling instant the daemon child was `state=R`, `wchan=0`, with the `--out` FIFO NOT yet open — still inside Argon2id, which costs 151-175 ms while the sample landed at ~110 ms. The window that was actually measured was "100 ms after exec". The wallet leg happened to be correct (5 ms of work, so it was genuinely blocked), which is exactly how a timing coincidence passes for a property. **The gate now waits until `/proc/<pid>/wchan` names the FIFO rendezvous (`wait_for_partner`) before sampling** — the same thing the wallet leg was accidentally achieving — with the existing 25 s watchdog as the bound; if the child never blocks, the leg FAILS rather than banking a pass, and on a kernel that does not name the wait it prints `SKIP:` and banks nothing. Measured after the fix: the daemon leg samples at t+169..192 ms, `state=S wchan=wait_for_partner`, 5 runs of 5. **The proof that it was worth doing is mutant M9**, which writes the resolved passphrase into the argv block AFTER `envelope::encrypt` and `serialize` have run: RED against the synchronised gate, **GREEN against a byte-for-byte replica of the old timed one**. This is wave-doctrine lesson 16 — "for a 'the secret is absent from X' property, sample at or after the last moment the code could have put it there" — recorded one day earlier and repeated here anyway; recording a lesson is not the same as having learned it.

**What the D window still does not cover, said here rather than discovered later:** an argv write AFTER that `open(2)` returns, i.e. during the `--out` write or between it and exit. A FIFO can pin a process at an open and nowhere else. That residue is a few hundred microseconds of a code path that holds no secret, and it is not zero; the gate's header says so too.

Where `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` cannot be read the section prints `SKIP:` and banks nothing, and A, B and C still assert there; this is not a wrapper-level platform skip, because most of what it gates exists on every platform.

**The mutants — twelve, INCLUDING the two that came back GREEN, because a record that reports a cleaner result than the harness measured is worse than the defect it hides.** Each was verified to have reached BOTH the source and the RELINKED binary by a marker grep before any verdict was read; the harness refuses a verdict otherwise, and also refuses one if the build failed or the binary's mtime did not move. The transcripts are `/root/audit/z2/mutants/run.log`, `/root/audit/z2/fix/mutants-M7b-M10.log` and `/root/audit/z2/fix/B2-M9-two-windows.txt`.

RED: **M1** wallet argv-writeback after resolving `--priv-from` → D1. **M2** the named warning dropped → all eighteen C "raw warns" assertions, in both binaries, plus C37. **M3** an unopenable `file:` source accepted instead of refused → B. **M5** the both-at-once refusal dropped → B. **M6** a `file:` source resolving to the wrong value while every refusal still fires → A, and only A. **M7** the passphrase policy trimming whitespace like the hex policies → A5/A6/A10. **M8** daemon argv-writeback immediately after resolving `--passphrase-from` → D3. **M4b** `light/seed_source.hpp` binding `SEED_POLICY` to PASSPHRASE → five assertions of the UNCHANGED light gate. **M7b** `detail::normalize_value` trimming for every policy — the `env:`/`prompt` half of the no-trim rule, with the `file:` half left correct → A5b/A6b. **M9** the daemon writing the resolved passphrase onto argv AFTER the envelope is sealed and serialized → D3. **M10** the unknown-source refusal echoing the whole specifier again → B21b/B21c.

**GREEN, and each one is a finding this increment would otherwise not have made:**

* **M4** — `determ::light::seed_hex_from_source` made to forward on the PASSPHRASE policy instead of SEED. `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh` stayed green, exit 0, zero FAIL lines. The harness's own words are "THE GATE CANNOT SEE THIS MUTANT. That is a hole, not a pass." The cause is the finding: **after the promotion, three of the five `determ::light::` forwarders have NO CALLER inside `determ-light`** — `seed_hex_from_source`, `warn_seed_on_command_line` and `zero_secret_string` (verified by grep over `light/`: callers exist only for `resolve_seed_hex`, `zero_secret_bytes`, `SeedScrub` and `scrub_on_scope_exit`). An editor who opens `light/seed_source.cpp` to change one of those three bodies changes nothing, runs the gate, sees 28 green and believes light's behaviour moved. It did not. They are kept (they are the documented S-110 names and deleting declarations is not part of a behaviour-preserving move) and the fact is written into `light/seed_source.hpp` at the locus. M4 was then re-aimed as M4b at the one point that CAN still drift. **A mutant coming back GREEN is what found this; reading the code had not.**
* **M7** — GREEN on its FIRST run. The gate's password fixture was `'p a s s  w/ spaces'`, internal spaces only, so trimming was a no-op on it and the rule the mutant erased was invisible. The fixture now carries LEADING and TRAILING spaces, which is the case the passphrase policy exists for, and M7 is RED. The gate would otherwise have claimed to pin a rule it could not see.

Neither of those two facts survived into the first draft of this entry or the first draft of the S-114/S-115 ledger rows: both said "mutants M1-M8 RED", which silently renumbered M4b to M4 and deleted the GREEN M4 along with the three things it taught. Independent review caught it on 2026-09-18 and it is corrected here, in the ledger rows, and in the test-table row.

**Riders: none, and two things that look like riders are not.** (1) `wallet/main.cpp::passphrase_from_source` was re-pointed at the shared header rather than left as a third living copy — that IS the promotion, and this project has now recorded two separate incidents of hand-rolled copies of one primitive drifting inside two days. (2) **TEN** shipped test wrappers were edited, because the new warning is a stderr line and every capture of the form `X=$(cmd --password ... 2>&1)` that then parses the result as an ARTIFACT would have it folded into stdout. `2>/dev/null` is the wrong answer and the first cut of this increment used it; the claim that accompanied it — "no assertion was weakened or deleted" — was **measurably false**, and independent review measured it: against a shim that is the real binary plus ONE spurious stderr line (standing in for a future defect that reports on stderr and is not this warning), four of the ten went from RED to **fully GREEN** — `test_wallet_envelope_compat` 8 FAIL → 0, `test_wallet_message_sign` 9 → 0, `test_wallet_backup_create` 3 → 0, `test_account_encrypted` 2 → 0 — and four more lost assertions. Those captures were exact equalities and `json.loads` calls, so merged stderr had been an implicit "and stderr is empty" assertion on the command under test, and discarding the stream retired it.

**What shipped instead:** each of those captures uses the `--<name>-from` twin THIS INCREMENT ADDS and **keeps `2>&1`**. The secret comes off the command line, so no warning is printed at all, so there is nothing to discard. Measured after: every one of the ten is green against the real binary and RED against the one-line stderr shim at its pre-change FAIL count — envelope_compat 16 pass / 0 fail real and 7 FAIL / rc=1 shim, message_sign 9, keyfile_argon2 13, keyfile_create 9, operator_keyfile_kdf_audit 8, keyfile_recover 7, backup_create 3, account_recover 3, account_encrypted 2, rpc_auth rc=1 (it dies under `set -e` at the first JSON parse, exactly as it did before). No wrapper needed the fallback of filtering the warning line with `grep -v`. A side effect worth stating: ten shipped wrappers now exercise the NEW `-from` path on every run, which the suite otherwise barely covered.

Captures of an ERROR message deliberately still pass the RAW flag and still merge the two streams — they assert a diagnostic, and the raw flag continuing to work is itself under test. **The ten, and the count, corrected from the first draft:** they are ten wrappers and **29 converted captures**, not "eleven ... one token each" — the eleventh file in the diffstat is the NEW gate, and the per-wrapper counts are 1, 5, 4, 5, 7, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1 (`rpc-auth` alone is 7); **three** are FAST members — `test_operator_keyfile_kdf_audit`, `test_wallet_envelope_compat`, `test_wallet_keyfile_argon2` — and **seven** are not: `test_wallet_message_sign`, `test_wallet_rpc_auth`, `test_wallet_backup_create`, `test_wallet_keyfile_recover`, `test_wallet_account_recover`, `test_wallet_keyfile_create`, `test_account_encrypted`, found by running them by hand because nothing in CI does.

**What does not change.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no genesis field, no migration, no dependency. No secret's VALIDATION moved: hex length, charset and every existing refusal happen exactly where they did, which is what makes the equivalence assertion meaningful. No raw flag was removed or had its exit code changed. No file permission, no write path and no `--out` emitter was touched.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (a) `src/main.cpp` `cmd_account_address` (`determ account address <privkey_hex>`) and `cmd_send_anon` (`determ send_anon <to> <amount> <privkey_hex>`) take the private key as a POSITIONAL argument — `send_anon` is the one that SIGNS and submits. The `--<name>-from` convention does not map onto a positional without changing the command grammar, which would touch every shipped script that calls them; that is a separate increment and the S-115 row says so. (b) `src/main.cpp` `cmd_submit_param_change`'s `--keyholder-sig <idx>:<priv_hex>` carries a keyholder private key on argv; it is one repeated argument holding an index and a key, so it needs a list-valued source form of its own. (c) `wallet/main.cpp` `cmd_shamir_split` — the LEGACY positional `determ-wallet shamir split <secret_hex>`, still dispatched — takes the secret positionally, same reason as (a). (d) `wallet/main.cpp` `cmd_envelope_encrypt`'s `--plaintext <hex>` is the data being sealed and is still on argv. (e) `light/main.cpp`'s `rpc-auth --secret` is a same-class site in the third binary that S-110 did not cover and this increment does not enter. (f) `wallet/main.cpp` `cmd_merkle_proof`'s `--key-hex` was on the candidate list and is NOT a secret — it is a state-trie leaf key — so it was classified out, not converted. (g) `tools/test_wallet_rpc_auth.sh` has a PRE-EXISTING failing assertion, "canonical sorts params keys alphabetically": its needle is passed to `grep` as a basic regular expression in which `\"` matches a bare quote, while the JSON it searches carries a literal backslash. Measured here to fail identically with and without the new stderr line, so it is not this increment's doing; it is outside the FAST tier, which is why nothing had run it. Left alone as out of scope and named here so it is not lost. (h) `rpc-auth --json` renders a bad `--secret-from` source as a stderr line and exit 1 rather than through its `{"valid":false}` envelope, because the refusal is the shared primitive's and forking it for one call site would undo the point of the extraction; stdout stays clean either way and the help text says so. (i) **Three `determ::light::` forwarders have no caller after the promotion** — `seed_hex_from_source`, `warn_seed_on_command_line` and `zero_secret_string` (`light/seed_source.cpp`, declared in `light/seed_source.hpp`). Editing one of their bodies changes nothing `determ-light` executes and `tools/test_light_seed_source.sh` stays green; the one point light CAN still drift at is `SEED_POLICY`, which both live entry points share and which M4b pins. Found by mutant M4 coming back GREEN, not by reading. Kept, because they are the documented S-110 names and deleting declarations is not part of a behaviour-preserving move, and written into `light/seed_source.hpp` at the locus. (j) **The resolved secrets are not `determ_secure_zero`d at the eighteen call sites.** Not a regression — the raw path always copied `argv` into a `std::string` and never scrubbed it either, and `light/`'s own callers do scrub via `SeedScrub` — but the primitive exports `SecretScrub` precisely so a later pass can, and doing it here needs per-site lifetime analysis at eighteen sites. (k) **The header's `<windows.h>` include is NOT EXECUTED anywhere.** There is no MSVC or MinGW toolchain on this box. Review found that the include reaches `src/main.cpp` — a translation unit that had never seen `<windows.h>` before, and that has thirteen top-level `std::min`/`std::max` call sites after the include — so the header now defines `NOMINMAX` as well as `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN`, matching `src/net/iocp_detail.hpp:15-16` and `src/net/sync_client.cpp:23-24`, which carry the same guard with the same comment for the same reason. That is analysis plus the repo's own precedent; it is not verification, and the S-114 row says so. The comment at `src/main.cpp:141-155` that claimed the include had to follow the net headers "because winsock2.h must come first" was simply wrong — nothing above it includes `<winsock2.h>` — and is corrected. (l) **Four more non-FAST wrappers are RED at HEAD against correct code**, confirmed independently here and named so the next increment does not rediscover them: `tools/test_address_classify_fuzz.sh` (3 FAILs at `:115`, `:216`, `:232` — `account-derive-batch --out` writes a binary container that the wrapper `json.load()`s), `tools/test_wallet_snapshot_verify.sh` (20 FAILs from `:239` to the terminal marker at `:429` — its fixture is `{"version": 1}` and `snapshot inspect` now demands the DSN1 binary magic), `tools/test_pqauth.sh` (2, `:33` and `:40`, a python-oracle byte mismatch) and `tools/test_c99_vector_files.sh` (46 mismatches reported at `:1487`). `tools/test_wallet_shamir.sh` is FLAKY — review saw its tampered-share assertion fail once and pass five times; it was green 3 of 3 here — and it uses the legacy positional `shamir split <hex>`, which this increment deliberately left alone. None of the five is this increment's doing (the first two are JSON-to-binary container migrations that left a non-FAST wrapper behind; the last three are unrelated to argv), and none is fixed here: that is a separate increment. Together with (g) that is SIX guards that are red against correct code and that nothing runs — the same defect class this project has now hit three times.

**Verification:** `tools/ci_local.sh` on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, **RUN 328 / PASS 328 / FAIL 0 / PLATFORM-SKIP 0**, 16 doc guards green. The FAST tier moved 327 → 328 wrappers and the alternation 328 → 329 stems (`tools/run_all.sh` line 183); `docs/SECURITY.md` carries that figure in two places with the wrapper count, the stem count, the on-disk total and the per-platform sentence, and all four were moved together.

**Authority:** the standing verification doctrine in `CLAUDE.md`, and the S-110 entry of 2026-09-17, which named these sites as the deferred remainder of the class it opened. No owner decision is required or implied; removing the raw flags would be one, and is not done here.

## 2026-09-18 — the nine wallet outputs that never went through the restricted-write primitive, and one strace-ordering parser instead of three

**Status:** LANDED. Narrows `S-109` from `⚠ OPEN` to `🟠 Partially mitigated` and opens `S-116`. Changes `wallet/main.cpp` write paths, two test wrappers, and adds one shared parser file. No consensus code, no wire format, no daemon, no `light/`. Opens no new FAST wrapper, so the FAST count does not move.

**Problem, reproduced by EXECUTION at the pre-change binary built from `372e863` before anything was touched.** Wave 4 extracted `determ::util::write_restricted_0600` and routed the wallet's ten key-material writers through it. NINE other wallet outputs were left on the shape that primitive exists to remove, and the S-109 row named every one of them. Six ran `std::ofstream` -> write -> `std::filesystem::permissions` -> `(void)perm_ec`: the file is created at 0666 masked by the umask, the COMPLETE artifact is written into it, and only then is it narrowed. Measured under `umask 000` with `strace` and with a PASSIVE `LD_PRELOAD` observer that forwards every mode-setting call to libc unchanged and reports the file's real mode and size at the instant the narrowing is attempted: `cold-sign --out` `was=0644 size=425`, `sign-anon-tx --out` `was=0666 size=432`, `tx-batch-sign --out` `was=0644 size=419`, `param-change-build --out` `was=0666 size=567`, `backup-create --envelopes-out` `was=0644 size=269`, `account-import-many --summary` `was=0644 size=351`. Two of those are world-WRITABLE, not merely world-readable, for the duration of the write. The strace order is `openat(..., O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666)`, `write(...)`, `fchmodat(..., 0600)` at all six, and the FINAL mode is 0600 at all six — which is exactly why every after-the-fact check in this tree was green the whole time, including this gate's own outcome section. The other three narrowed NOTHING: no mode-setting call ever named them, and under `umask 000` they ended at 0666 permanently — `create-recovery --out` (the DRS1 container of password-wrapped share envelopes) and the `encrypt-message` / `decrypt-message --out` pair through a second, unhardened byte writer; `decrypt-message --out` is the recovered PLAINTEXT. Transcripts: `/root/audit/z3/REPRO-pre-372e863.txt`, `/root/audit/z3/REPRO-post-z3.txt`.

**The change, and why it is one new renderer rather than one new writer.** All nine now call the shared primitive through `wallet/main.cpp::write_file_0600_quiet`. It is NOT a second copy of the mechanism — it is one call into `determ::util::write_restricted_0600` — and it exists because the wallet's existing renderer, `write_bytes_file_0600`, hard-wires three things its ten callers share and these nine do not: Windows BINARY mode, its own diagnostic strings, and the P-2 reporting shape. Six of the nine write through a TEXT-mode `std::ofstream`, and "routing them through the binary helper would change their Windows bytes" is precisely the reason the S-109 row gave for leaving them there. The primitive's `windows_binary` knob removes that reason: passing false makes its Windows arm `std::ofstream f(path, std::ios::trunc)`, which is byte-for-byte the default-constructed stream those sites used. The three that had no permission call at all also pass `final_narrow=false`, so no by-path chmod is ADDED on a platform that never had one, and on POSIX that call would be redundant with the `fchmod` and is the TOCTOU shape the primitive exists to avoid — the same reasoning `src/crypto/keys.cpp::save_node_key` records for passing false.

**What this deliberately does NOT fix, stated here rather than left to be discovered.** The P-2 half stays open at all nine sites: `final_ec` is discarded exactly as `(void)perm_ec` discarded it, and a failed pre-write `fchmod` still warns nobody. Closing it means a new stderr line and a new `perms_narrowed` field across six commands and four `--json` contracts — a behaviour change to shipped output on every one of them, which is its own increment and not a rider on a window fix. The S-109 row says so and stays open for it.

**Three behaviour changes come with the primitive and cannot be opted out of; each is measured.** (1) `::close` is now CHECKED at the six sites that let the `ofstream` destructor close the file, so an ENOSPC/EIO flush failure is no longer exit 0 on a truncated artifact; the caller's existing "write failed" diagnostic renders it. (2) A failed write or close REMOVES the file instead of publishing a fragment under the final name — the rule both other restricted writers already state at their locus. (3) `O_NOFOLLOW`: a symlink at `--out` now fails instead of being written through. This is the same change the wallet's other ten outputs took on 2026-09-17, and it is an **OPERATOR-VISIBLE EXIT-CODE CHANGE ON NINE SHIPPED COMMANDS**, not only an attacker scenario. Stated in full here because the wallet increment of 2026-09-17 made this exact change without documenting it and had to be corrected the next day (this file: the 2026-09-17 integration entry at `:4829`, and the 2026-09-18 daemon entry at `:4863` whose "the wallet increment made the same change without documenting it and had to be corrected the next day" is the adjudication), and the accepted remedy is in the tree at `src/main.cpp:346` and `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md:53`. As an attack: at the pre-change binary 425 bytes of a signed envelope, 303 bytes of a DRS1 container and 68 bytes of message ciphertext each landed at an attacker-chosen link target with exit 0 and an empty stderr. As an operator break, measured PRE vs POST at the two binaries across all nine: **(a) `--out /dev/stdout` goes exit 0 to exit 1 on SEVEN of the nine** — unconditionally on the four that have no already-exists check (`account-import-many --summary`, `create-recovery --out`, `encrypt-message --out`, `decrypt-message --out`), and whenever `--force` bypasses that check on `backup-create --envelopes-out`, `cold-sign --out` and `tx-batch-sign --out`. `sign-anon-tx --out` and `param-change-build --out` do not move only because their exists-check already refused `/dev/stdout`. A `determ-wallet create-recovery ... --out /dev/stdout | gpg -c` pipeline loses its 303 bytes of DRS1 and gets exit 1. **(b) A DANGLING symlink fails on ALL NINE** — the legitimate `ln -s dated-2026-09-18.json out.json; cmd --out out.json` idiom — including the five with an already-exists check, because `fs::exists()` is false through a dangling link. **(c) `--out` inside a SYMLINKED DIRECTORY is UNCHANGED**, exit 0 at both binaries: `O_NOFOLLOW` guards the FINAL path component only, so an attacker who controls a parent directory is not stopped by it and this increment does not claim otherwise. **(d) `account-import-many --summary` now has two more ways to exit 1 AFTER both per-record keyfiles are already written at 0600 and NOT removed** — a partial success reported as a failure. That shape is PRE-EXISTING and is not caused by `O_NOFOLLOW`: measured at BOTH binaries, a `--summary` naming a directory exits 1 with `rec1.keyfile` and `rec2.keyfile` already in `--out-dir`. It is therefore DOCUMENTED rather than restructured — making the summary fail first would mean opening it before the records it describes exist, which is a different command. `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` now carries one note naming all nine commands and all four consequences, plus the `create-recovery` row. **(4) The refusal says WHY** — added after review, and the reason this whole change is survivable for an operator: `wallet/main.cpp::write_file_0600_quiet` discarded the `errno` the primitive captures, so an `ELOOP` on nine commands printed a bare "cannot open --out for write: <path>" on a path `ls -l`, `touch` and `test -w` all call fine. It now hands the caller the same `": " + strerror` SUFFIX its sibling `write_bytes_file_0600` has always rendered and that `include/determ/util/restricted_write.hpp` asks every caller for at its `err` field — a suffix on a line each site already printed, never a new line, and no exit code, stdout or `--json` field moves.

**Everything else is byte-identical, measured rather than argued.** With fixed keys the pre- and post-change binaries produce byte-for-byte identical `cold-sign`, `sign-anon-tx`, `tx-batch-sign`, `param-change-build`, `account-import-many --summary`, `account-import-many` per-record keyfiles and `decrypt-message` outputs; identical exit codes, stdout and stderr on nine success paths and on fourteen failure paths (eight parent-directory refusals and six where a DIRECTORY at the `--out` path drives the writer's open-failure arm); and the four randomised containers keep their exact lengths, with a `create-recovery` container written by either binary read back correctly by the other. Transcript: `/root/audit/z3/REPRO-bytes-parity.txt`, 32 same / 0 different before the `strerror` suffix of behaviour change (4) was added; re-measured after it, `/root/audit/z3/fix/PARITY-post-strerror.txt`, **24 same / 8 different** — the eight are open-failure STDERR lines and differ ONLY by the appended reason (three `: No such file or directory`, five `: Is a directory`). No on-disk byte, no exit code and no stdout differs anywhere.

**Second, independent defect in the same half: the strace-ordering parser existed in THREE copies.** `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` section A carried it as an inline heredoc, section C generated a second copy as `ordered.py`, and `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh` carried a third as `order_verdict`. Three copies of a security parser drift, and this one already had: a descriptor-only spelling scores `create 0600; fchmod(fd,0600); chmod(path,0666); write; chmod(path,0600)` as CLOSED with the window fully open, and every final-mode assertion in this tree passes on that trace. There is now ONE, `tools/strace_order.py`, enumerating `chmod` / `fchmod` / `fchmodat` / `fchmodat2` and asserting both clauses — at least one mode-setting call exists before the first write AND the last one sets 0600 — plus the rename-publish clauses section C needs and the strip-and-reparse non-vacuity self-check all three carried. Equivalence was MEASURED, not assumed: each removed copy and the survivor were run over the same real traces the originals were exercised with (shamir-split over a pre-existing 0644 target, `account-import-many` records 2 and 3, the `keyfile-rotate` staged temp with its rename, and both branches of `determ account create --out`) plus the two negative shapes, 12 comparisons, identical assertion outcome, 0 divergent. Transcript: `/root/audit/z3/REPRO-parser-parity.txt`.

**The gate.** `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh` was EXTENDED, not duplicated: **50 to 101 assertions**, FAST (its stem is already in the `ONLY_PATTERN`, so the FAST wrapper count does NOT move), 0 sections skipped on this box. New **section F** runs an ordering leg per site over `strace`; seven of the nine run against PRE-EXISTING 0644 targets, and `sign-anon-tx` and `param-change-build` refuse an existing `--out` and have no `--force`, so their only path is a fresh create and the section says that in its own output rather than implying coverage it does not have. **Section D** gained nine outcome assertions run under `umask 000`, so a 0600 result means the mode was SET and not inherited from a friendly umask, plus a tenth asserting the table of nine was actually walked — a site that silently stopped running would otherwise bank no assertion and no failure. New **section E** gates the ORDERING PARSER itself over synthetic traces with known answers, including the exact drift trace above; it needs no strace, no ptrace, no compiler and no binary, so it runs on Darwin and the BSDs where A, C and F can only skip. New **section G**, added after review, gates the `O_NOFOLLOW` exit-code change ITSELF — nothing in this tree did — with two clauses at each of the nine sites: a dangling symlink at the output path is REFUSED and nothing is written through it, and the refusal NAMES ITS REASON on stderr rather than printing the path alone. A dangling link is used because it is the one shape that reaches the open at all nine; G needs only symlink support, so like E it runs where A, C and F cannot. Section F's eighteen assertions are NINE verdicts about the wallet plus NINE parser non-vacuity self-checks which are green against a defective wallet too (M1 fails one assertion there, not two) — the section now says so in its own output so the count is not read as eighteen checks on `determ-wallet`. The wrapper's summary line keeps its single unconditional marker and its `pass_count > 0` floor. Its Windows platform-skip text is corrected: it claimed section E "rests on a POSIX file mode", which is false — E is pure python over hand-written trace strings and needs no mode, no strace and no binary. E is unreachable on Windows only as a side effect of the wrapper-level exit that happens before it, and the consequence is now stated there: the single shared security parser has ZERO gate coverage on Windows. Moving E above that exit would fix it and would change the per-platform assertion count `docs/SECURITY.md` states in prose, which another track is editing this wave, so it is named rather than done.

**Mutants.** Ten, each planted one at a time, each RED. Transcripts `/root/audit/z3/MUTANTS-cpp-v2.txt` and `/root/audit/z3/MUTANTS-tools-v2.txt`. The harness REFUSES to report a verdict unless a marker grep proves the mutation reached the source AND — for a C++ mutant — the RELINKED binary; for a tool-only mutant it proves the marker is in the exact file the gate invokes and says that no link step happened rather than implying one.

| id | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `cold-sign --out` alone reverted to create-then-narrow | RED — 98 pass / 3 fail: that site's section F ordering assertion plus both of its section G clauses (reverting the site also reverts its `O_NOFOLLOW`) |
| M2 | the pre-write `::fchmod` dropped from the shared primitive | RED — 82 pass / 19 fail |
| M3 | `chmod(path, 0666)` inserted between the narrowing and the first write | RED — 85 pass / 16 fail; every final-mode assertion in the tree stays green and only the ordering parser sees it |
| M4 | `write_file_bytes` reverted to the un-narrowed `ofstream` | RED — 93 pass / 8 fail (section F, section D and both section G clauses at `encrypt-message` and `decrypt-message`) |

| M6 | the parser's non-vacuity self-check stops stripping | RED — 86 pass / 15 fail |
| M7 | one of the nine sites quietly dropped from the gate's table | RED — 95 pass / 1 fail (the walked-the-table assertion) |
| M8 | a bare `except: pass` planted in `tools/strace_order.py` | RED — judged by a DIFFERENT gate, `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh`, 51 pass / 1 fail, the D4 hit naming `tools/strace_order.py` and the planted line (no line number is quoted here: the line exists only in the mutant); this is what proves D4 now reaches the de-duplicated parser, which `ls tools/test_*.sh` could not see |

**A consequence of the de-duplication, found by review and fixed here: the surviving parser had fallen out of the only ratchet that scans for a vacuous python verdict.** `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh` D1/D2/D3 sweep `ls tools/*.sh` and D4 sweeps `ls tools/test_*.sh`; a standalone `tools/strace_order.py` matches neither, and D4 reads python HEREDOCS, which a `.py` file does not contain. So moving the parser out of three shell heredocs moved it out of the ratchet entirely. D4 now also reads a whole `.py` file as one body and sweeps `tools/strace_order.py` explicitly. It is NOT extended to all `tools/*.py`: twenty of the twenty-six are invoked by a gate wrapper and sweeping them turns D4 RED today on ELEVEN bare `except: pass` hits in four files — `tools/rpc_tamper_proxy.py:189,:198,:200,:219`, `tools/verify_d5rp.py:122,:132,:144,:154,:169`, `tools/verify_enote.py:331` and `tools/verify_view_key.py:178`. Those are reference verifiers and a tamper proxy, not gate verdict computers; the boundary is the same one the `tools/operator_*.sh` exclusion already draws, and the eleven are listed in D4's own comment with file:line so the next increment starts from a list. `tools/test_gates_can_fail.sh` stays at 52 assertions.

**Riders: none.** Files changed: `wallet/main.cpp` (write paths only — the argument parsers and their usage text are untouched), `tools/test_wallet_out_perms.sh`, `tools/test_account_create_perms.sh`, the new `tools/strace_order.py`, `docs/SECURITY.md` and this log.

**What does not change.** No consensus accept rule, no apply path, no wire format, no digest, no genesis field, no migration, no RPC, no `light/`, no daemon source. No container format changes: `keyfile-recover --out` still writes raw bytes and `keyfile-decrypt --out` still writes the daemon's unframed `node_key.json`, both recorded in S-116 rather than changed. No `--json` contract gains or loses a field. No exit code changes except the `O_NOFOLLOW` refusal named above, which IS an exit-code change on nine shipped commands and is documented as one. `tools/run_all.sh:183` is NOT touched.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** **(1)** `tx-history-export` (`wallet/main.cpp::cmd_tx_history_export`, the open at `:19220`, the by-path chmod at `:19231`) and `account-balance-history` (`wallet/main.cpp::cmd_account_balance_history`, `:19690` and `:19698`) open their `--out` with a bare `ofstream` and chmod it BY PATH afterwards. What they do was **re-measured** before this entry was written, because two earlier drafts of this item were wrong about it and the review caught both. They do NOT leave a complete export readable for the duration of the write: under `strace`, `umask 000`, at the committed binary, both are `openat(AT_FDCWD, "<out>", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0666) = 3` immediately followed by `chmod("<out>", 0600) = 0` with NO `write(3, ...)` between them — final mode 600, final size 0. That ordering is structural: the open is deliberately done before any RPC chatter so an unwritable destination fails fast, and every row is emitted after the RPC connect. The residual there is a short EMPTY-FILE window plus a by-path (TOCTOU) chmod. And there is no recorded decision to defer to: `cmd_account_balance_history` has NO comment at that site at all, and the only comment, at `tx-history-export` (`:19228-19230`), says that a chmod FAILURE does not fail the export — the P-2 question, not the P-1 window. **The actual reason they are left is about the code:** both sinks are a STREAMING `std::ostream` flushed per line for `tail -f` friendliness, while `determ::util::write_restricted_0600` is a ONE-SHOT blob writer taking a pointer and a length. The primitive does not fit, and nothing in this tree bridges a restricted descriptor to a `std::ostream` — `grep` for `stdio_filebuf` and `fdopen` across the repo returns nothing. **What IS worth naming at those two sites, demonstrated here and strictly worse than the window the earlier draft described: they FOLLOW SYMLINKS.** Neither open carries `O_NOFOLLOW` and the chmod is by path, so a `--out` pointing at a symlink truncates and re-modes the TARGET — measured, a `victim.txt` at mode 644 with 27 bytes became mode 600 with 0 bytes, and `account-balance-history` did the same to a second file (27 bytes to 0). Transcript: `/root/audit/z3/REMEASURE-th-sites.txt`. Anyone who can plant a symlink in the output directory gets an arbitrary truncate plus an arbitrary chmod-to-0600 on any path the invoking user can write. It is PRE-EXISTING; this increment neither caused nor widened it. It is NOT closed here, and that is a decision with a stated cost: closing it race-free needs a restricted descriptor bridged into a streaming `std::ostream`, which on libstdc++ means `__gnu_cxx::stdio_filebuf` and on MSVC has no standard equivalent — a portability decision, plus a tenth and eleventh command taking the `O_NOFOLLOW` exit-code change, plus its own gate; a four-line pre-open `lstat` refusal would be cheap but is defeated by a race, and shipping a racy check as a fix for a TOCTOU is worse than naming the gap. S-109 carries the measurement and the file:line. **(2)** The remaining `std::filesystem::permissions` call in `wallet/main.cpp::cmd_keyfile_rotate` (`:4372`, post-rename) is NOT of this class and is untouched: it narrows an inode the staging write already created at 0600, its `error_code` IS checked, and on Windows it is the only narrowing there is. **(3)** `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh` carries its own ordering parser TWICE, at `tools/test_node_key_perms.sh:202` and `:249`. It is a different parser, not a fourth copy of the de-duplicated one — it scopes its window by the descriptor's CLOSE rather than by the first write, hardcodes the `node_key.json` suffix instead of taking a target, and answers `closed`/`open` rather than a mode — and it already enumerates all four mode-setting spellings, so it does not carry the drift this increment removed. Porting it onto the shared interface changes what that gate asserts and belongs in its own increment; the note is written into `tools/strace_order.py` so the next reader finds it. **(4)** `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` now carries ONE note, at the end of the "Wallet diagnostic CLIs" section, documenting the symlink refusal and its four consequences for the NINE commands this increment migrated — placed at the end of that section deliberately, so that no line inside its table moves and the `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md:638` citations at `:2976` and `:2978` of THIS append-only file are left exactly as they were (`:2978` was already four rows off before this increment; not touched, and not made worse). What is still NOT documented: the same refusal on the wallet's other TEN outputs migrated on 2026-09-17, and the wallet USAGE TEXT for all nineteen. The usage text is the other half of `wallet/main.cpp` and belongs to another track this wave, so the nine lines it needs are handed to the integrator rather than written here; the shape to copy is `src/main.cpp:346`, "a --out naming a SYMLINK is refused, not written through". `determ-wallet sign-anon-tx` has no row of its own in the reference at all, which is why the note names the commands explicitly instead of annotating rows. **(5)** `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md:629` documents `keyfile-recover` with three flags the binary rejects and an output format it does not produce — measured, not inferred — and that is the second half of S-116.

## 2026-09-18 — wave 5 integration: three tracks landed, and the derived state a three-way merge invalidates

**Status:** landed. Three increments (`track/z1`, `track/z2`, `track/z3`), each green and adversarially reviewed on its own base, cherry-picked serially onto `master` and reconciled.

**PROBLEM.** Landing three independently verified increments does not give a verified tree. Three classes of state in this repo are derived from the whole tree, so each track computed them correctly against its own base and every one of them was wrong once merged.

(1) **The FAST count.** z1 and z2 each added exactly one wrapper and each re-derived the prose from 327 to 328. A merge that takes either side asserts 328 over a tree of 329 — and takes it in the same sentence the 2026-09-17 doctrine already records as having gone stale twice. The figures are now derived once, by computation over the merged tree rather than by arithmetic on the sentence: 330 stems in the `ONLY_PATTERN` alternation, 573 `tools/test_*.sh` on disk, 329 matched, one stem (`dsso_assertion`) with no wrapper, 329 asserting on Linux and macOS and 327 on Windows. `tools/run_all.sh` carries the union of both tracks' stems, checked for duplicates and for losses in both directions.

(2) **The `docs/SECURITY.md` §1 summary cells.** Three tracks moved five ids between rows. Recomputed from id MEMBERSHIP, not from the numerals: Open (untouched) 3/14/10/7 = 34 (S-112 out by z1, S-109 out by z3, S-116 in by z3); Partially mitigated 1/1/5/2 = 9 (S-114 and S-115 in by z2, S-109 in by z3); Mitigated in-session 19/26/5/12 = 62 (S-112 and S-113 in by z1). Every numeral is asserted equal to the count of distinct S-ids in its own cell and every row total to the sum of its four cells. This matters most for the "Partially mitigated" row, which `tools/test_security_ledger_coherence.sh` does not derive at all — it checks id membership for "Open (untouched)" and "Reopened" only, and reads no numeral anywhere. A wrong merge in that row lands silently, which is why it was checked by hand and why z2's own pass recorded the gap at the locus.

(3) **`file:line` citations into the two files two tracks edited.** z2 added 104 lines to `src/main.cpp` and 32 to `wallet/main.cpp` ahead of loci that z1 and z3 cite. Ten citations introduced by this wave were verified against the merged tree; six pointed at the wrong construct and are corrected: `cmd_genesis_tool_build` `src/main.cpp:5468`→`:5503` and its `--json`-only argv scan `:5475`→`:5511` (z1's named residual); the symlink-refusal wording `src/main.cpp:329`→`:346`, cited twice as the shape to copy (z3); the corrected include comment `src/main.cpp:144`→`:141-155` (z2); and the two audit exports `wallet/main.cpp` `:19220`/`:19231`→`:19252`/`:19263` and `:19683-19699`, `:19690`/`:19698`→`:19715-19732`, `:19722`/`:19730` (z3). Each corrected line was then read back and asserted to contain the construct it names. `tools/test_doc_citation_bounds.sh` cannot catch this class: it checks only that a cited line is at or below EOF, and every one of these was.

**The reviews.** Each track was reviewed by an independent agent that did not write it. **All three returned NOT SAFE**, with nine blockers, every one fixed and re-verified before landing: z1's headline property was false inside the verb the increment is named after (`enqueue` gates its whole nonce-reservation block on `have_nonce`/`have_port`, so three flags stayed accept-and-ignore after the fix) and its new gate hard-coded the flag universe it claimed to derive; z2's daemon process-table window sampled the child during Argon2id rather than after the seal, ten shipped wrappers had lost stderr coverage to accommodate a new warning line, the records asserted eight RED mutants when the harness had measured one GREEN, a summary cell did not sum, and `<windows.h>` newly reached `src/main.cpp` without `NOMINMAX` ahead of thirteen `std::min`/`std::max` sites; z3's record described a write window that measurement showed was already closed and deferred to an in-code comment that does not exist at one of the two sites, and `O_NOFOLLOW` broke `--out /dev/stdout` on nine shipped commands undocumented — the same omission this log records as having had to be corrected the next day once before.

**What does NOT change.** No consensus rule, no wire format, no on-disk byte of any container. The reconciliation touched `tools/run_all.sh`'s stem list, three summary rows, one derived paragraph and ten citations; it changed no code.

**Noticed and deliberately left alone, with the locus.** (a) Six non-FAST wrappers are RED against correct code at this commit and nothing in `ci_local` runs them: `tools/test_wallet_rpc_auth.sh:183` (1), `tools/test_address_classify_fuzz.sh:115,:216,:232` (3), `tools/test_wallet_snapshot_verify.sh:239-:429` (20), `tools/test_pqauth.sh:33,:40` (2), `tools/test_c99_vector_files.sh:1487` (46), and `tools/test_wallet_shamir.sh` flaky. Confirmed independently by two agents, not caused by this wave, and named rather than fixed — this is the third time this project has found a guard red for weeks because nothing ran it. (b) Three wrappers flaked once each under three-agent contention and passed on re-run: `tools/test_fa_partition_virtual.sh` (fixed ports 7651-7655, twice), `tools/test_mempool_admit_affordability.sh` (exit 143), and one unexplained single failure of `tools/test_light_outbox.sh` section E that did not reproduce in 300 consecutive runs of the exact invocation. The fixed-port binding is a real hazard for concurrent runs on one box. (c) Every residual each track named in its own entry stands; none was closed by the merge.

**Verification:** `bash tools/ci_local.sh` at this commit on Linux x86_64 — build 7 targets, `RUN: 329 / PASS: 329 / FAIL: 0 / PLATFORM-SKIP: 0`, `SKIP: 2` of the 329 passing wrappers declined at least one section with 0 of those asserting nothing, 16 offline doc-coherence guards green, 0 `FAIL` lines anywhere in the log. Counts re-derived by computation over the merged tree, not copied. Log at `/root/audit/wave/ci_z_integrated.log`.

**Authority:** owner-directed wave, three tracks in parallel worktrees, independent adversarial review of each, integrator reconciliation. Passing tests are not proof of regulatory compliance and nothing here claims a class is closed while sites of the same class remain named above.

## 2026-09-20 — consensus & validator landing: quorum intersection (D5a/S-054), exit unlock (D7/S-067), anon small-order rejection (D10/S-072), sync hardening (S-080/S-085), block frame cap (D9/S-057), and open validator set (D6/S-069)

**Status:** landed.

**What landed:**
1. **D5a / R-4 (S-054) — Quorum intersection $2K > N(h)$ over the eligible pool per shard:**
   - Genesis: `GenesisConfig::validate()` enforces `2K > |initial_creators|`.
   - Selection: `BlockValidator::check_creator_selection` and `Node::check_if_selected` assert $2K > |nodes|$ fail-closed.
   - Admission: `BlockValidator::check_transaction` rejects `TxType::STAKE` from any domain if the resulting eligible pool would reach or exceed $2K$ (`current_eligible + 1 >= 2 * k_block_sigs_`).
   - Gated by leg GB-8 in `test-genesis-binary-codec` and `test-block-validator-extensive`. S-054 fully mitigated.

2. **D7 / R-11 (S-067) — Exit and unlock path:**
   - In `BlockValidator::check_transaction`, sender verification admits `TxType::UNSTAKE` from an inactive domain present in `chain.registrants()` once `block_index >= chain.stake_unlock_height(tx.from)`, authenticated via its registered `ed_pub`.
   - All other transactions from inactive domains remain rejected.
   - Gated by `test-unstake-deregister-apply`. S-067 mitigated.

3. **D10 / R-13 (S-072) — Anonymous small-order curve point rejection:**
   - Transactions where the anonymous sender address decodes to an 8-torsion curve point are rejected in `BlockValidator::check_transaction` (top-level and batch inner), `Node::verify_tx_signature_locked`, and `Chain::apply_transactions`.
   - Wallet and light client outbox refuse/warn on sends to small-order addresses.
   - Gated by `test-anon-small-order-key` and `tools/test_anon_small_order_key.sh`. S-072 mitigated.

4. **S-080 & S-085 (D19a / D19b-i) — Sync hardening and storm suppression:**
   - `MAX_SYNC_LEAD = 100,000` bound enforced in `Node::on_status_response` to reject remote hit-and-run height claims. Disconnected peers are pruned.
   - `Node::start_sync_if_behind` unicasts `GET_CHAIN` directly to `best_addr` with a 5-second in-flight suppression window, and clamps recorded peer heights on un-advancing responses.
   - Gated by `test-sync-storm-and-lead-bound` and `tools/test_sync_storm_and_lead_bound.sh`. S-080 and S-085 mitigated.

5. **D9 / R-7 (S-057) — Canonical block frame consensus cap & non-PQ `pq_auth` rejection:**
   - `BLOCK_FRAME_CONSENSUS_CAP_BYTES = (4 * 1024 * 1024) - 4` (4,194,300 bytes) declared in `include/determ/chain/params.hpp`.
   - `BlockValidator::validate` enforces that any block whose encoded canonical frame exceeds `BLOCK_FRAME_CONSENSUS_CAP_BYTES` is invalid.
   - `Producer::build_body` packs transactions, inbound receipts, and shard-tip records up to the cap, preserving relayability over the 4 MB wire envelope.
   - Non-PQ transactions with non-empty `pq_auth` are rejected at ingress (`Node::verify_tx_signature_locked`), block verification (`BlockValidator::check_transaction`), and inner batch checks.
   - Gated in `test-block-validator-extensive`. S-057 mitigated.

6. **D6 / R-12 (S-069) — Open validator set join path:**
   - `BlockValidator::check_transaction` admits `TxType::STAKE` and `TxType::TRANSFER` from a domain present in `chain.registrants()` before it reaches the eligible floor (`block_index < it->second.inactive_from`).
   - Combined with D5a, `STAKE` cannot exceed the quorum intersection bound $2K > N(h)$.
   - Gated in `test-block-validator-extensive`. S-069 mitigated.

7. **D8 / R-14 (S-073) — Zeroth pool unseeded default:**
   - Genesis default `zeroth_pool_initial = 0` eliminates zero-cost NEF pool drainage. S-073 mitigated.

**Verification:**
- Full local CI suite: `bash tools/ci_local.sh` passing all 329 test wrappers, 0 failures, 16 doc coherence and tier checks green.
- Ledger coherence guard: `bash tools/test_security_ledger_coherence.sh` PASS (27 OPEN rows, 0 REOPENED rows, summary counts derived).

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D5a, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D19a, D19b-i (DECISION-LOG 2026-09-16).

## 2026-09-20 — storage integrity (S-084), light-client quorum floor (S-100), bounded egress (S-082), and anonymous CT ingress parity (S-065)

**Status:** landed.

**What landed:**
1. **D19a (S-084) — Storage integrity & hash continuity on reload:**
   - In `src/chain/chain.cpp`, `Chain::load` and `Chain::export_store_json` validate sequential block index continuity (`b.index == i`) and cryptographic hash linking (`b.prev_hash == (i == 0 ? Hash{} : prev_hash)` where `prev_hash` is the recomputed hash of block $i-1$).
   - Mismatched or non-linking blocks throw `std::runtime_error`, rejecting corrupted block files fail-closed.
   - Gated by `test-chain-store` (CS-11: corrupted `prev_hash` and corrupted `index` both rejected) and `tools/test_chain_store.sh`. S-084 mitigated.

2. **D19a (S-100) — Light-client quorum downgrade check on inclusion proofs:**
   - In `light/verify_tx_inclusion.cpp`, `verify_tx_inclusion_from_block` passes `genesis.k_block_sigs` and `genesis.bft_enabled` to `verify_block_sigs`.
   - Blocks with fewer creators than required by genesis ($K$-of-$K$ in MD mode) are rejected as `InclusionVerdict::UNVERIFIABLE`.
   - Gated by `determ-light selftest-tx-inclusion-height` and `tools/test_light_verify_tx_inclusion_height.sh`. S-100 mitigated.

3. **D19a (S-082) — Bounded peer egress write queue:**
   - Declared `MAX_PEER_WRITE_QUEUE = 256` in `include/determ/net/peer.hpp`.
   - In `src/net/peer.cpp`, `Peer::send` checks write queue backlog: if `write_queue_.size() >= MAX_PEER_WRITE_QUEUE`, it terminates the connection via `conn_->close()` without enqueuing further bytes, preventing unbounded memory growth from slow or non-reading peers.
   - `Peer::do_write` clears the backlog when an async write completes with an I/O error (`ec != 0`).
   - Gated by `test-sync-storm-and-lead-bound` (harness saturates queue to 256, verifies 257th message closes peer and halts deque growth) and `tools/test_sync_storm_and_lead_bound.sh`. S-082 mitigated.

4. **S-065 anon ingress arm — Anonymous transaction mempool ingress parity:**
   - In `src/node/node.cpp`, `Node::verify_tx_signature_locked` admits anonymous `SHIELD`, `UNSHIELD`, `CONFIDENTIAL_TRANSFER`, `ROTATE_AUDIT_KEY`, `LOG_AUDIT_ACCESS`, and `REGISTER_NOTE_KEY` matching `BlockValidator::check_transaction` rules.
   - Eliminates the client-facing rejection where `determ-light build-shield` submissions were dropped at gossip and RPC ingress.
   - Gated by `test-anon-small-order-key` (asserts honest anonymous `SHIELD` is admitted to mempool while unpermitted anonymous `STAKE` is dropped) and `tools/test_anon_small_order_key.sh`.

## 2026-09-20 — D19a (S-097): BlockValidator precheck in rpc_submit_tx landed

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED and verified. Gate `determ test-rpc-validator-precheck` (and wrapper `tools/test_rpc_validator_precheck.sh`). Ledger row S-097 moved from OPEN to MITIGATED in `docs/SECURITY.md`.

**Problem:**
Previously, `Node::rpc_submit_tx` verified the address canonical format, checked for hash mismatch, verified stale nonces, checked the signature via `verify_tx_signature_locked`, and checked mempool admission policy (`mempool_admit_check`). However, it did not execute `BlockValidator::check_transaction`. As a result, structurally invalid transactions (e.g. `TRANSFER` carrying payload > 128 bytes, anonymous accounts attempting unauthorized transaction types such as `STAKE`, malformed `STAKE`/`UNSTAKE` payloads, or amount + fee arithmetic overflows) were admitted into `tx_store_` and acknowledged to the RPC client as `{"status": "queued"}`. When the block producer later assembled a block via `Node::build_body` / `tx_admit_locked`, `check_transaction` rejected and evicted the transaction silently. From the RPC client's perspective, the transaction appeared accepted/submitted, until the light client outbox later diagnosed it as permanently STUCK.

**The Change:**
In `src/node/node.cpp::rpc_submit_tx`, immediately after the `mempool_admit_check(tx)` check:
```cpp
    const uint64_t at = chain_.empty() ? 1 : chain_.height();
    auto reg = NodeRegistry::build_from_chain(chain_, at);
    if (auto val_res = validator_.check_transaction(tx, at, chain_, reg, tx.nonce); !val_res.ok) {
        throw std::runtime_error("submitted tx rejected by validator (S-097): " + val_res.error);
    }
```
Passing `expected_nonce = tx.nonce` ensures that future-nonce transactions in the mempool pipeline (`tx.nonce >= chain_.next_nonce(tx.from)`) are NOT falsely rejected by the validator's nonce equality check, preserving mempool pipelining while still enforcing all structural, typing, payload-bound, and cryptographic rules.

**Verification & Test Gate:**
- Subcommand `test-rpc-validator-precheck` added to `src/main.cpp`.
- Test wrapper `tools/test_rpc_validator_precheck.sh` added and registered in `tools/run_all.sh` (`ONLY_PATTERN`).
- Evaluated scenarios:
  1. Setup: Genesis applied (height 1), mempool empty.
  2. CONTROL 1: Validly-signed `TRANSFER` from `node0` to `bob` (nonce 0, amount 10, fee 1) -> admitted (`queued`, `mempool == 1`).
  3. CONTROL 2: Future-nonce `TRANSFER` (nonce 1) -> admitted (`queued`, `mempool == 2`), verifying pipelining works.
  4. NEGATIVE 1: `TRANSFER` with oversized payload (129 bytes > `TRANSFER_PAYLOAD_MAX` 128) -> throws `runtime_error` containing `"submitted tx rejected by validator (S-097)"` and `"TRANSFER payload exceeds 128-byte cap"`, mempool remains 0.
  5. NEGATIVE 2: `STAKE` from anonymous account -> throws `runtime_error` containing `"submitted tx rejected by validator (S-097)"` and `"unauthorized tx type for anonymous account"`, mempool remains 0.
  6. NEGATIVE 3: `STAKE` with malformed payload size (4 bytes instead of 8) -> throws `runtime_error` containing `"submitted tx rejected by validator (S-097)"` and `"STAKE payload must be 8 bytes"`, mempool remains 0.
- Mutant verification:
  - Disabling the S-097 validator pre-check in `rpc_submit_tx` causes all three NEGATIVE arms to fail RED (invalid transactions return status `queued` with mempool incremented).

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D19a (DECISION-LOG 2026-09-16), node-local backlog Step 11.

## 2026-09-20 — D19a (S-075): Snapshot bootstrap with partial header tail preserves chain following

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED and verified. Gate `determ test-snapshot-partial-header-tail` (wrapper `tools/test_snapshot_partial_header_tail.sh`). Ledger row S-075 moved from OPEN to MITIGATED in `docs/SECURITY.md`.

**Problem:**
Finding S-075 (pre-existing, reproduced 2026-09-15, `docs/SECURITY.md` row S-075):
`Chain::height()` was previously defined as `blocks_.size()` and `Chain::at(i)` indexed `blocks_` positionally (`blocks_[index]`). However, snapshots in production carry only a trailing window of headers (`headers` array in JSON / DSN1, defaulting to 16 and capped at 256). When a node bootstrapped from a snapshot with a partial header tail:
1. `height()` returned `blocks_.size()` (e.g. 2 or 16) instead of the absolute head block index + 1 (e.g. 7 or 1000).
2. `at(index)` threw `std::out_of_range` on any absolute block index `>= blocks_.size()`.
3. `start_contrib_phase` initialized with `block_index = chain_.height()` (e.g. 2 instead of 7), and `apply_block_locked` treated legitimate incoming next blocks (index 7) as distant future stragglers (`b.index > height()`), refusing to validate or apply them. The node became permanently stuck and unable to follow consensus.
4. On node restart, `Node::Node` persisted in-memory blocks starting at index 0 (`0.blk`, `1.blk`), overwriting block files with the partial tail headers. This corrupted the local block store, causing `Chain::load` to fail on subsequent restarts with "block index mismatch".

**The Change:**
1. In `include/determ/chain/chain.hpp` and `src/chain/chain.cpp`:
   - Added `base_index_{0}` tracking the absolute block index of the first retained block in `blocks_`.
   - Updated `height()` to return `base_index_ + blocks_.size()`.
   - Added `base_index() const`, `tail_count() const`, and `has_block(uint64_t index) const`.
   - Updated `Chain::at(uint64_t index)` to check `index < base_index_ || index >= base_index_ + blocks_.size()` and return `blocks_[index - base_index_]`.
   - Updated `Chain::restore_from_snapshot` and `Chain::decode_state` to set `base_index_ = blocks_.front().index` (or `block_index + 1` if tail is empty).
2. In `src/net/binary_codec.cpp`:
   - Updated `encode_snapshot_response_frame` to check `tail_count() > kSnapshotHeaderMax` instead of `height() > kSnapshotHeaderMax`.
3. In `src/node/node.cpp`:
   - Guarded incremental block persistence (`save_incremental`) to only run if `chain_.base_index() == 0`, preserving the canonical snapshot seed on disk when running with a partial tail.
   - Updated `current_epoch_rand` to check `chain_.has_block(epoch_start - 1)` and fall back to `committee_checkpoints()` if pruned.
   - Guarded equivocation checking in `apply_block_locked` with `chain_.has_block(b.index)`.
   - Guarded RPC handlers (`rpc_status`, `rpc_chain_stats`, `rpc_block`, `rpc_headers`, `rpc_tx`, `rpc_chain_summary`, `rpc_dapp_messages`, and subscriber catch-up) and gossip handler `on_get_chain` with `chain_.has_block(...)`.
4. In `src/node/validator.cpp` and `src/node/shardtip_verify.cpp`:
   - Updated `resolve_epoch_rand` and anchor reading to check `chain.has_block(...)` before calling `chain.at(...)`.

**Verification & Test Gate:**
- Implemented test gate `determ test-snapshot-partial-header-tail` in `src/main.cpp` and bash wrapper `tools/test_snapshot_partial_header_tail.sh`.
  - Built a 7-block chain (blocks 0..6), serialized with `header_count = 2` (blocks 5 and 6).
  - Restored via both JSON (`restore_from_snapshot`) and binary DSN1 (`decode_state`).
  - Verified `height() == 7`, `head().index == 6`, `base_index() == 5`, `tail_count() == 2`.
  - Verified `at(5)` and `at(6)` resolve correctly, while `at(4)` and `at(7)` throw `out_of_range`.
  - Appended block 7: verified `height() == 8`, `head().index == 7`, `tail_count() == 3`, `has_block(7) == true`.
- Mutant falsification: reverting `height()` to `blocks_.size()` caused 7 test assertion failures and exited 1 RED against the rebuilt binary.
- Full local CI suite `tools/ci_local.sh` clean (359 wrappers asserted, 1 skipped entirely, doc/ledger guards green).

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D19a (DECISION-LOG 2026-09-16), node-local backlog Step 11.

## 2026-09-20 — D19a (S-098): Light-client state persistence durability via durable_write_replace

**Context & Defect Analysis:**
Finding F-3 (outbox review 2026-09-16, `docs/SECURITY.md` row S-098):
`save_light_state` (`light/persist.cpp`) previously opened the destination anchor cache path using a plain truncating `std::ofstream(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc)`. If a process crash, power loss, or unhandled exception occurred mid-write, the existing cache file was truncated or left in a partial state, resulting in loss of the cached committee-verified anchor (forcing re-sync from genesis on next invocation).

**Remedy (D19a / S-098):**
Replaced the plain truncating ofstream with `determ::light::outbox::durable_write_replace(path, out)` from `light/outbox.hpp`.
The write pipeline guarantees crash-durability and atomic replacement:
1. Data is written to temporary file `path.<pid>.tmp` at mode 0600.
2. File data and metadata are flushed to stable storage via `full_fsync` (`F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS / `fsync` on POSIX / `FlushFileBuffers` on Windows).
3. Temporary file is atomically renamed over the destination `path` (`rename(2)` / `MoveFileExW`).
4. On POSIX, the containing directory descriptor is opened and `full_fsync`'d to persist directory entry linkage.
5. If any step fails before rename, the temporary file is unlinked and the pre-existing anchor cache at `path` remains completely intact and valid.

**Verification & Test Gates:**
- In-binary check added to `determ-light state --selftest` (check 9):
  - Injects write failure via `DETERM_LIGHT_OUTBOX_INJECT=write_fail`.
  - Asserts `save_light_state` throws error.
  - Asserts the pre-existing anchor cache file at `tp` is NOT truncated or destroyed and remains readable with its original `head_height`.
- CLI & pipeline test added to `tools/test_light_state.sh` Section (E):
  - Asserts full trace event stream (`fsync_file`, `publish`, `fsync_dir`) is produced under `DETERM_LIGHT_OUTBOX_TRACE`.
- Mutant falsification:
  - Reverting `save_light_state` to bare `ofstream` fails both gates RED (no trace events emitted and/or pre-existing anchor is truncated on failure).

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D19a (DECISION-LOG 2026-09-16), node-local backlog Step 11.

## 2026-09-20 — D19a (S-099): Light-client read_account_trustless false-alarm TAMPERED eliminated (finding F-4)

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED and verified. Gate `determ-light selftest-outbox-hint-wait` (and wrapper `tools/test_light_outbox_flag_surface.sh`). Ledger row S-099 moved from OPEN to MITIGATED in `docs/SECURITY.md`.

**Problem:**
Finding F-4 (outbox review 2026-09-16, `docs/SECURITY.md` row S-099):
Previously, `read_account_trustless` in `light/trustless_read.cpp` performed operations in the following order:
1. Checked local state cache against `min_height`.
2. Fetched the Merkle `state_proof` for `("a:", domain)`.
3. Verified the proof against local key-bind and Merkle sibling rollup.
4. Called `committee_bound_state_root` to transitively bind the proof's `state_root` to the committee-signed successor block. If `max_wait_seconds > 0` was specified (e.g. `verify-and-submit --wait` or `outbox reconcile --wait`), this held and polled until a successor block was minted.
5. AFTER the successor wait completed, called `account` RPC to fetch the cleartext `balance` and `next_nonce`, recomputed the SHA-256 leaf hash, and compared it against `proof["value_hash"]`.

When the chain minted a successor block during the wait that touched the sender's account (e.g., the sender's own transaction landed in that successor block, or incoming funds were credited), the `account` RPC returned post-block state (new nonce/balance) while the `state_proof` was held from the anchor block. The hash recomputation mismatch triggered a false-alarm `TAMPERED` exception on an entirely honest daemon. While `outbox_cli.cpp` had added a band-aid `with_f4_retry` wrapper, the underlying library reader itself remained vulnerable.

**The Change:**
In `light/trustless_read.cpp::read_account_trustless`:
- Moved the `account` cleartext RPC call and value-hash verification to run immediately alongside `state_proof` (step 3), BEFORE calling `committee_bound_state_root`.
- Enclosed the (state_proof, account) dual-read in a bounded 3-attempt retry loop to handle the benign race where a block lands between the individual `state_proof` and `account` RPC calls.
- Both the Merkle proof and the cleartext fields are guaranteed to match the exact same anchor block view prior to entering `committee_bound_state_root`.
- When `committee_bound_state_root` polls and discovers the successor block, the successor attests to the anchor block's `state_root` and previous hash. Even if the sender's nonce advanced in the successor block, the anchor block's cleartext is already captured and verified, returning the correct account view without false-alarm `TAMPERED`.
- Retained strict syntactic key-bind checks (`proof_key_hex != local_key_hex`), stale-read guards (`proof_height < vc.height`), and value-hash cross-checks (`computed_value_hash != proof_value_hash`) to satisfy all invariants in `tools/test_light_keybind_surface.sh`.

**Verification & Test Gate:**
- Extended `determ-light selftest-outbox-hint-wait`:
  - Added test leg 3: simulated successor block landing during hold-and-wait with sender nonce advance (`live_node_account_read = true`, `auto_mint_consumes_nonce = true`). Asserts `read_account_trustless` with `--wait 2` completes cleanly without throwing `TAMPERED` and returns the anchor block's state.
  - Added test leg 4: simulated inter-call race where nonce advances between `state_proof` and `account` calls (`race_account_once = true`). Asserts the reader's bounded retry loop re-reads both calls and succeeds on attempt 2.
- Re-ran `tools/test_light_outbox_flag_surface.sh` (65 passed, 0 failed, 5 declined).
- Re-ran `tools/test_light_keybind_surface.sh` (invariants 4-10 exact).
- Re-ran `tools/test_light_state_root_binding_guard.sh` (invariants 1-3 intact).
- Verified mutant falsification: reading `account` cleartext after the wait immediately fails leg 3 RED with `TAMPERED`.

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D19a (DECISION-LOG 2026-09-16), node-local backlog Step 11.

## 2026-09-20 — D18a (S-063): DApp delivery layer apply reporting and value gating

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED and verified. Gate `determ test-dapp-delivery-apply-status` (and wrapper `tools/test_dapp_delivery_apply_status.sh`). Ledger row S-063 moved from OPEN to MITIGATED in `docs/SECURITY.md`.

**Problem:**
Finding S-063 (`docs/SECURITY.md`, log `8b86d39`/`0fe6eda`):
`make_dapp_call_frame` and `rpc_dapp_messages` stamped `amount` and `fee` from the raw transaction into every delivered frame. The DAPP_CALL block validation arm checks recipient/topic framing only, `build_body` performs no provisional debit, and delivery never consulted the transaction's actual apply result. As a result, an underfunded sender (e.g. zero balance) could submit a transaction that entered a block but skipped execution, while the node's delivery layer erroneously reported that the payment was made.

**The Change:**
1. **Chain Execution Tracking:**
   - In `Chain::apply_transactions`, tracked exact per-transaction execution status (`applied[tx_idx] = true` on successful balance/debit/credit apply, `false` on underfunded/skipped).
   - In `Chain`, stored `tx_applied_` parallel to `blocks_` across all state lifecycles: atomic append, `revert_head()` (depth-1 reorg), snapshot creation and restore (`restore_from_snapshot`, `decode_state`), and store reload (`Chain::load`).
   - Exposed `bool Chain::is_tx_applied(uint64_t index, size_t tx_index) const` for lockfree and synchronous status queries.
2. **Delivery Layer Apply Status & Value Gating:**
   - In `make_dapp_call_frame` (`src/node/node.cpp`), added `bool applied` parameter. Set `"status": applied ? "APPLIED" : "SKIPPED"`.
   - Gated `"amount"` and `"fee"` fields: stamped into JSON frame iff `applied == true`, and completely omitted iff `applied == false`.
   - Updated `Node::rpc_dapp_messages`, `rpc_dapp_subscribe` catch-up replay, and `on_block_finalized_for_subscribers` live push to query `chain_.is_tx_applied(h, t)` and pass it into frame construction.

**Verification & Test Gates:**
- Added CLI gate `determ test-dapp-delivery-apply-status` and wrapper `tools/test_dapp_delivery_apply_status.sh` asserting 28 test conditions across three arms:
  - Arm 1: `make_dapp_call_frame` JSON framing, status strings, amount/fee presence/omission.
  - Arm 2: `Chain::is_tx_applied` exact accounting across `DAPP_REGISTER`, underfunded `DAPP_CALL` (skipped), funded `DAPP_CALL` (applied), balance deltas, and `revert_head()` depth-1 reorg behavior.
  - Arm 3: `Node::rpc_dapp_messages` end-to-end delivery through disk store `save_incremental` and `Chain::load` replay, verifying `SKIPPED` without amount/fee on underfunded tx and `APPLIED` with amount/fee on funded tx.
- Mutant falsification:
  - M1: Unconditional inclusion of `amount`/`fee` in `make_dapp_call_frame` turns Arm 1 and Arm 3 RED.
  - M2: `Chain::is_tx_applied` returning `true` unconditionally turns Arm 2 and Arm 3 RED.
- Registered in `tools/run_all.sh` `ONLY_PATTERN`.

**Authority:**
Owner decisions D18a (DECISION-LOG §4151), node-local backlog Step 10.
